sections.translation_zh:
The Open Group 是一个全球性联盟，通过在900多家成员组织之间建立协作、包容和相互尊重的文化，借助技术标准与开源倡议推动业务目标的实现。成员来自多个行业，包括客户、系统与解决方案供应商、工具供应商、集成商、学术机构和顾问。

The Open Group 的使命是推动实现无边界信息流（Boundaryless Information Flow™），具体通过：

- 与客户合作，收集、理解并应对当前和新出现的需求，制定政策并分享最佳实践。
- 与供应商、联盟和标准组织合作，形成共识、促进互操作性，演进并集成规范和开源技术。
- 提供完整的服务集合，提高联盟的运营效率。
- 开发并运行业界领先的认证服务，鼓励采购经过认证的产品。

更多信息见 www.opengroup.org。The Open Group 出版广泛的技术文档，多数着眼于标准与指南的制定，也包括白皮书、技术研究、认证与测试文档，以及业务类出版物。详情见 www.opengroup.org/library。

source_units.text_en: The Open Group

The Open Group is a global consortium that enables the achievement of business objectives through technology standards and open source initiatives by fostering a culture of collaboration, inclusivity, and mutual respect among our diverse group of 900+ memberships. Our membership includes customers, systems and solutions suppliers, tool vendors, integrators, academics, and consultants across multiple industries.
The mission of The Open Group is to drive the creation of Boundaryless Information Flow™ achieved by:
• Working with customers to capture, understand, and address current and emerging requirements, establish policies, and share best practices
• Working with suppliers, consortia, and standards bodies to develop consensus and facilitate interoperability, to evolve and integrate specifications and open source technologies
• Offering a comprehensive set of services to enhance the operational efficiency of consortia
• Developing and operating the industry’s premier certification service and encouraging procurement of certified products
Further information on The Open Group is available at www.opengroup.org.

The Open Group publishes a wide range of technical documentation, most of which is focused on development of Standards and Guides, but which also includes white papers, technical studies, certification and testing documentation, and business titles. Full details and a catalog are available at www.opengroup.org/library.

sections.translation_zh:
TOGAF® 系列指南说明如何使用TOGAF标准，以及如何调整它以满足具体需要。

系列指南预期是TOGAF标准中发展最快的部分，定位为标准的指导部分。TOGAF基础内容预期保持长期稳定，而使用指导可以针对行业、架构风格、用途和问题。例如，支持扩展企业转型所需的利益相关者、关注点、视图和支撑模型，可能与将内部IT环境迁移到云所需的内容显著不同；两者都使用ADM，都从架构愿景开始，开发目标架构，并走向实施与迁移计划。TOGAF基础内容仍是跨行业、领域和风格的必要支架。

source_units.text_en: About the TOGAF® Series Guides
The TOGAF® Series Guides contain guidance on how to use the TOGAF Standard and how to adapt it to fulfill specific needs.

The TOGAF® Series Guides are expected to be the most rapidly developing part of the TOGAF Standard and are positioned as the guidance part of the standard. While the TOGAF Fundamental Content is expected to be long-lived and stable, guidance on the use of the TOGAF Standard can be industry, architectural style, purpose, and problem-specific. For example, the stakeholders, concerns, views, and supporting models required to support the transformation of an extended enterprise may be significantly different than those used to support the transition of an in-house IT environment to the cloud; both will use the Architecture Development Method (ADM), start with an Architecture Vision, and develop a Target Architecture on the way to an Implementation and Migration Plan. The TOGAF Fundamental Content remains the essential scaffolding across industry, domain, and style.

本指南的作者兼具企业架构与项目管理背景。

（请注意：以下所属机构为批准时的信息。）

**Jacek Presz**

Jacek Presz（linkedin.com/in/jacekpresz）是一位经验丰富的企业架构师，专注于规划并支持技术驱动的业务转型。他曾在银行、科技以及电力与公用事业公司担任首席企业架构师。在一家领先咨询公司任职期间，他为不同行业的客户交付了战略层面与分段层面的架构项目。他积极参与 TOGAF® 标准的制定。

**Łukasz Wrześniewski，The Open Group 受邀专家**

Łukasz Wrześniewski（linkedin.com/in/lukaszwrzesniewski）是一名敏捷转型与企业架构顾问，专长于敏捷企业架构与敏捷项目群管理（Agile Program Management）。他也是一名活跃的培训师，讲授 TOGAF®、ArchiMate®、IT4IT™ 与 Scaled Agile 课程。他以受邀专家（invited expert）身份参与敏捷企业架构团队，以及架构、IT4IT、ArchiMate 协调项目（Harmonization Project）。

**Łukasz Drążek，PMP**

Łukasz Drążek，PMP（linkedin.com/in/lukaszdrazek）是一名经理，在银行、公共部门、能源、电力与公用事业以及快速消费品（FMCG）行业的大型 IT 项目方面拥有经验。他专长于项目与项目群管理（project and program management）、项目群挽救（program recovery）、技术驱动的转型以及变革管理。他负责 EY 波兰 Digital & Technology Enablement Advisory Group 的 IT 交付管理（IT Delivery Management）业务。

**Maciej Iwaniuk，PMP**

Maciej Iwaniuk，PMP（linkedin.com/in/maciekiwaniuk）是一名认证项目经理，也是经验丰富的项目审计师，拥有本地及国际项目的规划、执行与管理经验。他参与项目管理方法的设计、开发与实施。他是 EY EMEIA Advisory Center 的集成负责人（Integration Leader）。

**Bartłomiej Rafał，EY**

Bartłomiej Rafał（linkedin.com/in/bartlomiejrafal）是 TOGAF 认证从业者，也是 EY 波兰 Digital & Technology Enablement Advisory Group 的高级分析师。在 EY 任职期间，他参与了面向全球领先组织的一些规模最大的架构转型项目群。目前，他致力于提升自身的企业架构技能（尤其是数据与应用领域），并将其用于支持有意开展数字化转型的组织。

**Filip Szymański，EY**

Filip Szymański（linkedin.com/in/szymanskifilip）是 TOGAF 认证从业者，也是一名经理，在领导以企业架构为核心的战略性与战术性变革管理项目方面拥有经验。他专长于设计企业架构，以及旨在使能业务价值交付的信息系统架构。他负责 EY 波兰 Digital & Technology Enablement Advisory Group 的 IT 架构（IT Architecture）业务。

**Piotr Papros**

Piotr Papros（linkedin.com/in/papros）是一名 IT 经理，在领导面向全球性机构的复杂 IT 项目、项目群与服务方面拥有经验。他是精益敏捷（Lean-Agile）项目群顾问，曾在组织层面的转型工作中担任精益敏捷教练。他热衷于游戏化、企业变革管理与体育运动。

The authors of this Guide have backgrounds in both Enterprise Architecture and Project Management.
(Please note affiliations were current at the time of approval.)
Jacek Presz

Jacek Presz (linkedin.com/in/jacekpresz) is an experienced Enterprise Architect focused on planning and supporting technology-enabled business transformation. He has held Chief Enterprise Architect positions in Banking, Technology, and Power & Utilities companies. While working for one of the leading consulting firms, he delivered Architecture Projects on a strategic and segment level for clients in different sectors. He is actively engaged in TOGAF® Standard development.
Łukasz Wrześniewski, The Open Group Invited Expert

Łukasz Wrześniewski (linkedin.com/in/lukaszwrzesniewski) works as an Agile Transformation and Enterprise Architecture Consultant. He specializes in Agile Enterprise Architecture and Agile Program Management. He is also an active trainer who provides TOGAF®, ArchiMate®, IT4IT™, and Scaled Agile training courses. He is participating in the Agile Enterprise Architecture team and in the Architecture, IT4IT, ArchiMate Harmonization Project as an invited expert.
Łukasz Drążek, PMP

Łukasz Drążek, PMP (linkedin.com/in/lukaszdrazek) is a manager with experience in largescale IT projects for the banking, public, energy, power & utilities, and FMCG sectors. He specializes in project and program management, program recovery, technology-enabled transformation, and change management. He is responsible for the IT Delivery Management practice in the Digital & Technology Enablement Advisory Group, EY Poland.
Maciej Iwaniuk, PMP

Maciej Iwaniuk, PMP (linkedin.com/in/maciekiwaniuk) is a certified Project Manager and experienced Project Auditor with experience in local and international project planning, execution, and management. He is involved in Project Management method design, development, and implementation. He is an Integration Leader at EY EMEIA Advisory Center.
Bartłomiej Rafał, EY

Bartłomiej Rafał (linkedin.com/in/bartlomiejrafal) is a TOGAF Certified practitioner and a Senior Analyst in the Digital & Technology Enablement Advisory Group, EY Poland. During his career at EY, he has been involved in some of the largest architecture transformation programs for leading organizations around the world. Currently, he is interested in improving his Enterprise Architecture skill set (especially in data and application domains), and applying it to support organizations intending to undergo Digital Transformation.
Filip Szymański, EY

Filip Szymański (linkedin.com/in/szymanskifilip) is a TOGAF Certified practitioner and a manager with experience in leading strategic and tactical change management projects focused around Enterprise Architecture. He specializes in designing Enterprise Architecture, as well as information systems architectures aimed at enabling value delivery to the business. He is responsible for the IT Architecture practice in the Digital & Technology Enablement Advisory Group, EY Poland.
Piotr Papros

Piotr Papros (linkedin.com/in/papros) is an IT Manager experienced in leading complex IT projects, programs, and services for worldwide institutions. He is a Lean-Agile program consultant, having served as a Lean-Agile coach in transformation efforts at an organization level. He is an enthusiast of gamification, enterprise change management, and sport.

source_units.text_en: 1. Introduction

sections.translation_zh:
架构项目本质上通常很复杂，需要恰当的项目管理才能保持正轨并兑现承诺。本文档面向负责规划与管理架构项目的人员，说明如何用 PRINCE2 或 PMBOK 等事实标准补充 TOGAF 架构开发方法（ADM），以强化项目管理、提高架构项目成功概率。

本文档为架构项目团队提供总体视图与详细指导：哪些 PRINCE2 或 PMBOK 的流程、工具与技术可与 TOGAF ADM 配合用于项目规划、监控与控制；并给出 TOGAF 框架流程与交付物同 PRINCE2、PMBOK 的详细映射，以可视化这些概念如何结合。

本文档并非项目管理方法教科书：它说明架构项目应采用哪些项目管理工具与技术，具体技术细节以 PRINCE2 与 PMBOK 出版物为准。

我们希望把项目管理技术引入架构项目，以成熟、专业的方式提高交付价值与解决方案的成功概率，支持 The Open Group 的“无边界信息流”愿景。

source_units.text_en: 1.1. Overview

Architecture Projects are typically complex in nature. They need proper Project Management to stay on track and deliver on promise. This document is intended for people responsible for planning and managing Architecture Projects. We explain how the TOGAF® Architecture Development Method (ADM) [C220] can be supplemented with de facto methods and standards such as PRINCE2® [PRINCE2] or PMBOK® [PMBOK] to strengthen Project Management and improve the probability of success for Architecture Projects.

This document provides Architecture Project Teams with an overall view and detailed guidance on what processes, tools, and techniques of PRINCE2 or PMBOK can be applied alongside the TOGAF ADM for project planning, monitoring, and control. Further, a detailed mapping of the processes and deliverables of the TOGAF Framework against PRINCE2 and PMBOK is provided to visualize how those concepts come together.

This document is not intended to serve as a Project Management method guidance book. We explain what Project Management tools and techniques should be applied to Architecture Projects, but we rely on specific PRINCE2 and PMBOK publications for detailing those techniques or tools.

We hope that the introduction of Project Management techniques to Architecture Projects will improve the chances for success of delivered value and solutions in a mature and professional way, supporting The Open Group vision of Boundaryless Information Flow™.

按 TOGAF 标准，企业架构是企业组件的结构、组件间相互关系，以及治理其设计与随时间演进的原则与指南。企业是组织的最高描述层级，通常覆盖所有使命与职能，可跨越多个组织。

TOGAF 标准包含架构开发方法（ADM），旨在成为开发与实施企业架构的行业标准方法；该方法聚焦架构产品的交付。在 TOGAF 标准中，架构产品通过执行 ADM 所述任务交付；任务分组为相互关联的阶段，每阶段包含若干步骤。完成一个 ADM 周期可能很复杂，因此架构产品交付常以项目形式执行。

“架构项目”并非 TOGAF 标准定义的术语，但常用于指为定义并描述待实施企业架构而开展的项目。本文档中，“架构项目”涵盖阶段 A 至 F 及需求管理中的所有活动。


图1-1：架构项目与TOGAF ADM的关系（改编自TOGAF标准）。

阶段 A–F 的关键成果是**架构定义文档**，描述将在阶段 G 实施、阶段 H 维护的企业架构。因此，阶段 F 结束时，待实施的企业架构已被定义与描述——按本文定义，架构项目即告完成。

**预备阶段、阶段 G、阶段 H 不在架构项目范围内**：预备阶段关注确保组织的企业架构能力；阶段 G 的目标是治理企业架构的实施，通常作为独立工作（一个项目或一组项目）运行；阶段 H 的目标是维护已实施的企业架构，属于运营业务（或流程）而非项目管理。

source_units.text_en: 1.2. Background

According to the TOGAF Standard, Enterprise Architecture is the structure of enterprise components, their inter-relationships, and the principles and guidelines governing their design and evolution over time. Enterprise is the highest level of description of an organization and typically covers all missions and functions; it can span multiple organizations.

The TOGAF Standard includes the Architecture Development Method (ADM) that aims to be an industry standard method for developing and implementing an Enterprise Architecture. This method focuses on delivery of architecture products.

In the TOGAF Standard, architecture products are delivered through execution of tasks described in the ADM. These tasks are grouped into inter-related phases, each of which includes a number of steps. Completing an ADM cycle can be a complex task. Therefore, architecture products delivery is often executed as a project.

Architecture Project is not a term defined in the TOGAF Standard; however, it is used often for a project undertaken to define and describe an Enterprise Architecture to be implemented. Therefore, in this document, the term “Architecture Project” encompasses all activities undertaken within Phases A to F, and Requirements Management.
Figure 1-1: Architecture Project Relationship to the TOGAF ADM (Adapted from the TOGAF Standard)

A key result of Phases A to F is an Architecture Definition Document, which describes the Enterprise Architecture to be implemented in Phase G and maintained in Phase H. Therefore, at the end of Phase F the Enterprise Architecture to be implemented is defined and described — and the Architecture Project, by our definition, is completed.

The Preliminary Phase, Phase G, and Phase H are out of scope for the Architecture Project. The Preliminary Phase is concerned with ensuring an Enterprise Architecture capability of the organization. The goal of Phase G is to govern implementation of the Enterprise Architecture. Typically, it is run as a separate endeavor (a project or a set of projects). The goal of Phase H is to maintain the Enterprise Architecture implemented — it is related to operational business (or process) rather than project management.

sections.title_en: 1.3. Why do we need a Guide on Architecture Project Management?
sections.title_zh: 为什么需要架构项目管理指南？
sections.translation_zh:
TOGAF ADM 详细说明了企业架构开发各阶段的目标、方法、输入、步骤与输出，但对“如何管理一个架构项目”并未作具体规定，而是把这一问题留给聚焦项目管理的方法[1]。

项目管理是对项目各方面的计划、委派、监控与控制，并激励相关人员，以便在时间、成本、质量、范围、收益与风险的预期绩效目标内实现项目目标[2]。业界领先的项目管理方法包括 PRINCE2 与 PMBOK，它们可用于提高架构项目的成功概率。

并非所有 TOGAF 实践者都熟悉项目管理方法；即便是熟悉这些方法的实践者，也缺乏关于如何将 TOGAF 框架与这些方法结合使用的指导。

本文档旨在为 TOGAF 架构师提供如何管理架构项目的指南。我们建议以选定的项目管理技术补充 TOGAF ADM，其目标是通过更好的计划、监控与沟通提高架构项目的成功概率。

source_units.text_en: 1.3. Why do we need a Guide on Architecture Project
Management?

The TOGAF ADM details objectives, approach, inputs, steps, and outputs of the Enterprise Architecture development phases. However, it is not specific on how to manage an Architecture Project and leaves
that to methods that focus on Project Management.

Project Management is the planning, delegating, monitoring, and control of all aspects of the project, and the motivation of those involved, to achieve the project objectives within the expected performance targets for time, cost, quality, scope, benefits, and risks.[2] Market-leading Project Management methods include PRINCE2 and PMBOK. They can be used to enhance an Architecture Project’s chances of success.
Not all TOGAF practitioners are familiar with Project Management methods. Even for those who are, there is no guidance on how to use and align the TOGAF Framework with these methods.

The intent of this document is to provide guidelines for TOGAF architects on how to manage an Architecture Project. We suggest an approach that supplements the TOGAF ADM with selected Project Management techniques. The goal of this approach is to enhance an Architecture Project’s chances of success through better planning, monitoring, and communication.

source_units.text_en: 1.4. Document Scope and Structure
This document is structured in the following sections, with a specific target audience in each case:
• Chapter 2 describes a high-level Project Management approach for developing an Enterprise Architecture

The target audience for this section is Enterprise Architects, Project Management professionals, and stakeholders of Architecture Projects who want to understand the key relationships between the TOGAF Standard and Project Management areas.
• Chapter 3 describes a detailed Project Management approach for developing an Enterprise Architecture

It includes a step-by-step guide to Architecture Project initiating, planning, monitoring, and closing. The target audience of this section is Enterprise Architects who are familiar with the TOGAF Standard and who lead Architecture Projects.
• Chapter 4 and Chapter 5 present detailed mappings between the phases of the TOGAF ADM and PRINCE2 and PMBOK processes, respectively
These sections provide a foundation on which the guidance was built and are included for reference.

敏捷项目管理方法不在本文档的范围内。根据我们的经验，TOGAF 框架可以裁剪以采用敏捷方式，这种裁剪能够带来重要收益；但本文档不探讨这一主题。

**注释**

[1] TOGAF 标准——架构开发方法：阶段 A：架构愿景（建立架构项目）：“ADM 的每个周期通常都应作为项目，在企业既定的项目管理框架内实施。”

[2] 此处采用 PRINCE2 的定义。按更通用的 PMBOK 定义，项目管理是把知识、技能、工具与技术应用于项目活动，以满足项目的要求。

source_units.text_en: 1.5. Constraints

This document explores how Project Management methods can supplement the TOGAF ADM in Architecture Project delivery. It focuses on PRINCE2 and PMBOK as proven practices in the Project Management area.

Agile Project Management methods are out of scope for this document. In our experience, the TOGAF Framework can be tailored to use an Agile approach. Such tailoring can provide important benefits. However, it is not explored in this document.
Endnotes

[1] The TOGAF Standard — Architecture Development Method: Phase A: Architecture Vision (Establish the Architecture Project): “Each cycle of the ADM should normally be handled as a project using the project management framework of the enterprise”. [2] This is a PRINCE2 definition. According to the more general PMBOK definition, Project Management is an application of knowledge, skills, tools, and techniques to project activities to meet the project requirements.

sections.translation_zh:
架构项目是为定义并描述待实施企业架构而开展的工作。按 TOGAF 术语，它涵盖 ADM 阶段 A 至 F 及需求管理中的所有活动；实践中可以是独立项目，也可以是更大工作（如项目群）的一部分。




> 架构项目**不包含** ADM 的预备阶段、阶段 G 或阶段 H。预备阶段聚焦建立架构能力而非交付架构定义，必要时可发起架构项目（其输出，尤其“架构工作请求”，作为架构项目输入）。阶段 G（实施治理）关乎实施而非定义架构，可作为独立项目或项目群。阶段 H（变更管理）是维护架构并在必要时发起架构项目的持续过程，应作为运营活动对待。

架构项目以**架构工作请求**开始（按 TOGAF ADM，该请求是启动阶段 A 的输入），交付**架构定义、路线图与实施计划**；当这些输出移交实施时项目结束。

架构项目可涉及一个或多个架构域：TOGAF 定义业务、数据、应用、技术四个域，项目通常覆盖其中若干或全部。

图2-1：企业架构层级（TOGAF标准：架构全景概要分类模型）。

架构项目可涉及不同架构层级：TOGAF 定义三个层级，项目通常恰好覆盖其一：

- **战略层**：覆盖整个企业，定义整个企业架构的高层愿景、原则与战略方向；
- **分段层**：定义企业某分段（业务域）的企业架构；
- **能力层**：定义单个业务能力的企业架构，最详细，直接导向能力实施。

战略层架构项目通常作为分段层项目的输入；分段层项目又为能力层项目提供输入。

架构项目可作为独立工作或更大工作的一部分：

- **独立架构项目**通常作为单独项目执行（符合企业项目管理规定），有自身可独立实现的目标（架构定义而非其实施），常见于战略与分段层；
- **作为更大工作的一部分**：架构项目是项目或项目群的一部分，通常是工作流或一组任务，关键目标是为更大工作中的实施开发架构；常见于能力层，有时也在战略/分段层。此类架构工作不必按企业项目管理法规被认定为项目，更常见的是工作流或任务组。本指南的方法对两者均适用。

**表 2-1：架构项目示例**

| 总体目标 | 架构项目概述 |
|---|---|
| （A）评估现有应用组合并提出改进选项 | 描述应用全景并识别 IT 改进选项。约 50 个不同规模应用（精确数量待定，多为定制开发）。关键关注：确定应用间关系与数据流；映射应用能力（重叠与缺口）；识别应用开发的关键技术约束。所需视图待定；改进选项应包含带优先级的举措；时间框架可在最长 22 周的范围内灵活安排。 |
| （B）改进物流流程效率、缩短订单周期 | 对目标物流流程改进进行建模与规划：提供包裹位置、资源使用与流程瓶颈的当前信息；通过更准确的计划优化资源使用；通过更快资源分配与预分配资源缩短订单到交付时间。物流是运输公司的核心业务流程之一，三个大型业务单元起关键作用，每个又分约五个子单元。团队除一名业务分析师与一名企业架构师外，还包括一名已了解部分流程的主题专家。 |
| （C）整合近期合并企业的 IT 环境 | 定义目标 IT 架构及三年整合路线图。电力与公用事业控股公司含八个近期合并的业务单元，从事能源分销与销售，地域不同；业务相似但各有流程与 IT 应用，彼此不共享。架构项目目标是形成整合路线图，包含共性业务服务、IT 应用与基础设施；方法含现状分析、目标建模与路线图三阶段，须满足既定预算与时间约束。 |
| （D）为零售销售区新运营模式定义客户信息系统的解决方案架构 | 分析某电力与公用事业公司零售销售领域运营模式的变化及由此产生的解决方案架构需求；识别支持该领域的现有IT系统中阻碍新运营模式实施的问题；开发能够处理已识别问题并支持该运营模式的客户信息系统解决方案架构，同时绘制该系统与其环境中其他IT解决方案之间的数据交换图；编制包含该解决方案架构说明的客户信息系统招标文档。 |
| （E）新建弹性管理信息系统以满足银行报告需求 | 定义并实施新的弹性管理信息系统，满足不断扩大的银行报告需求并缩短信息延迟。范围包括：分析现状（旧数据仓库入/出接口、数据处理逻辑与报表类型）；定义目标架构（含把废弃功能迁移到其他方案）；准备高层设计文档。 |

示例覆盖的架构层级（战略 A/C、分段 B/D、能力 E）、架构域（业务 B/C/D/E，数据 B/C/D/E，应用 A/B/C/D/E，技术 C/D/E）与项目关系（独立 A/B/D、项目群一部分 C/E）各不相同。

表2-1的例子选取自现实架构项目，涵盖不同项目特征。这些例子将在第3章继续使用，以提供实践语境；引用这些项目的例子在原文中用灰底框表示。

source_units.text_en: 2.1. Architecture Project Definition

An Architecture Project is an endeavor undertaken to define and describe the Enterprise Architecture to be implemented. In TOGAF terms, as shown in Figure 2-1, it encompasses all activities undertaken within the Phases A to F and Requirements Management of the ADM. Practically, it can be a stand- alone project or part of a larger effort (e.g., a program).
An Architecture Project does not include the Preliminary Phase, Phase G, or Phase H of the ADM.

The Preliminary Phase focuses on establishing an Architecture Capability rather than delivery of an Architecture Definition. It can initiate an Architecture Project when necessary (outputs from the Preliminary Phase, especially Request for Architecture Work, are treated as an input to the Architecture Project).

Phase G (Implementation Governance) is about implementing the architecture, not defining it. It can be a separate project or a program (or even a part of the same program as the Architecture Project), but it is not concerned with delivery of an architecture (outputs from the Architecture Project are treated as inputs to Phase G).

Phase H (Change Management) is a continuous process concerned with maintaining the architecture and initiating Architecture Projects when necessary and it should be treated as an operational activity.

An Architecture Project starts with a Request for Architecture Work, which — according to the TOGAF ADM — is an input initiating Phase A. It delivers an Architecture Definition, a Roadmap, and an Implementation Plan. It is finished when these outputs are handed over for implementation.

An Architecture Project can concern one or more architecture domains. The TOGAF Standard defines four architecture domains (Business, Data, Application, Technology) — an Architecture Project typically covers a few or all of them.
An Architecture Project can concern different levels of architecture. The TOGAF Standard defines three levels of architecture — an Architecture Project typically covers exactly one of these:
• Strategic Level: covers the entire enterprise and defines the high-level vision, principles, and strategic directions for the entire Enterprise Architecture
• Segment Level: defines the Enterprise Architecture for a segment (business domain) of the enterprise
• Capability Level: defines the Enterprise Architecture for a single business capability
Enterprise Architecture at this level is the most detailed and leads directly to capability implementation.
Figure 2-1: Levels of Enterprise Architecture (the TOGAF Standard: Summary Classification Model for
Architecture Landscapes)

Architecture developed by an Architecture Project on the strategic level typically is an input to a segment-level Architecture Project. Similarly, segment-level Architecture Projects provide input for capability-level Architecture Projects.
An Architecture Project can be executed as a stand-alone endeavor or as part of a larger effort:
• A stand-alone Architecture Project is usually executed as a separate project (in line with the Project Management regulations of the enterprise)

It has its own set of goals that can be achieved by the project itself (i.e., the Architecture Definition not its implementation). Stand-alone Architecture Projects are often executed on the strategic and segment architecture level.
• Part of a larger effort means that the Architecture Project is a part of a project or program, typically a work stream or a group of tasks

Its key goal is to develop the architecture for implementation within the larger effort. Architecture Projects that are a part of a larger effort are usually executed on the capability architecture level and sometimes on the strategic and segment levels.

An Architecture Project that is a part of a larger effort does not have to be recognized as a project in terms of the Project Management regulations of the enterprise. More often, it can be a work stream or simply a group of tasks. The approach recommended in this document can be applied to both stand-alone Architecture Projects and architecture work that is part of a larger effort.

• Define target architecture including moving deprecated functionality to other solutions
• Prepare High Level Design documentation |
These examples were chosen to encompass different kinds of Architecture Projects. Generally, they can be characterized by:
• Levels of architecture[1] covered: Strategic (A, C), Segment (B, D), Capability (E)
• Architecture domains[2] covered: Business (B, C, D, E), Data (B, C, D, E), Application (A, B, C, D, E), Technology (C, D, E)
• Relationship to other projects: stand-alone (A, B, D), part of a larger program (C, E)
These project examples are used throughout Chapter 3 to enhance presented guidance with a practical context. Examples that refer to these projects are denoted using gray boxes.

sections.translation_zh:
架构项目可作为单个预先规划的阶段执行，但通常分为若干阶段：分阶段允许更灵活的方式，每个阶段通常在其开始前才详细规划（而非在项目开始时）。TOGAF 标准倡导迭代执行架构项目——此时每次迭代可视为一个独立阶段。

本文档将详细讨论项目的阶段划分。有关迭代方法，参见TOGAF标准——应用ADM：对ADM应用迭代。

架构项目包含以下可分组排序的管理活动：

- **项目启动**：任命执行发起人与项目经理、项目管理团队，汲取以往经验，选择项目方法，汇编项目任务书，规划下一阶段；
- **项目规划**：基于项目管理方法描述项目范围界定与规划活动；
- **阶段规划**：描述如何把架构项目划分为阶段，并按总体项目计划规划某阶段；
- **执行、监控与控制阶段**：描述如何用项目管理方法监控与控制 ADM 阶段 B–F 的架构开发活动；
- **阶段收尾**：描述阶段结束时执行的关键步骤；
- **项目收尾**（及架构交付物移交实施）：描述项目收尾活动、把架构项目产品移交给实施项目群/项目，以及经验教训记录方法。

上述序列构成架构项目生命周期，本文档以其为基本结构讨论架构项目管理。该生命周期映射到 TOGAF ADM（描述架构开发阶段与步骤），见图 2-2。


> 为简化，图中假定架构项目按类似 ADM 阶段的方式划分（每阶段对应一个 ADM 阶段）。实际情况通常并非如此，多数情况下也不应如此；TOGAF 标准推荐迭代方法，一个项目阶段可以覆盖若干 ADM 阶段，并可重复执行。

图2-2：从TOGAF ADM视角看架构项目生命周期。

本文档将详细讨论阶段划分；有关架构开发迭代，参见TOGAF标准——应用ADM：对ADM应用迭代。

架构项目生命周期也映射到项目管理方法。这些方法一般抽离项目实际的专业工作（即架构开发），聚焦于项目成功执行所需的管理流程与步骤。TOGAF ADM与常用项目管理方法的详细映射见第4章和第5章。

表 2-2 给出架构项目生命周期与 TOGAF ADM 阶段及项目管理方法的高层映射。请注意：TOGAF 标准聚焦架构项目中的架构开发活动，而项目管理方法聚焦如何管理这项工作的成功执行。

**表 2-2：架构项目生命周期映射到 TOGAF ADM 与项目管理方法**

| 架构项目生命周期 | TOGAF ADM 阶段 | PRINCE2 | PMBOK |
|---|---|---|---|
| 架构项目启动 | 阶段 A（架构愿景）——建立架构项目步骤 | 项目启动流程（Starting up a Project）——全部步骤 | 启动过程组：§4.1 制定项目章程；§13.1 识别利益相关者 |
| 架构项目规划 | 阶段 A（架构愿景）——制定架构工作说明书（Statement of Architecture Work）步骤及此前各步骤 | 发起流程（Initiation）——创建项目计划、汇编项目启动文档（Project Initiation Documentation） | 各过程组的规划过程——制定并汇总项目管理计划 |
| 阶段规划 | 无直接映射，但可视为前一阶段的收尾步骤 | PRINCE2 比 PMBOK 更强调项目阶段的概念。本文档所述概念主要基于 PRINCE2 流程，但也与 PMBOK 一致。 | 见共同说明 |
| 执行、监控与控制阶段 | 阶段 B–F 各阶段 | 本节（执行、监控与控制阶段）映射到 PMBOK 所定义的执行、监控与控制过程组。 | 见共同说明 |
| 阶段收尾 | 无直接映射，但可视为前一阶段的收尾步骤 | 见共同说明 | 见共同说明 |
| 架构移交 | 阶段 F（迁移规划）——收尾步骤 | 项目收尾流程（Closing a Project）——移交产品 | 项目收尾部分 |

（来源：改编自 TOGAF 标准、PRINCE2 与 PMBOK® 指南第 5 版）

架构项目生命周期由六类活动组成，可以映射到TOGAF ADM阶段以及项目管理方法的流程和步骤；第3章按此组织详细内容。

source_units.text_en: 2.2. Architecture Project Lifecycle

The Architecture Project can be executed as a single, preplanned stage, but usually it is divided into a few stages. Use of stages allows for a more elastic approach, as each of the stages is typically planned in detail just before it starts (rather than at the start of the whole project). The TOGAF Standard advocates iterative execution of Architecture Projects — in this case, each iteration can be considered a separate stage.

Dividing the Architecture Project into stages is discussed in detail in this document. For more information on the iterative approach, refer to architecture development in the TOGAF Standard — Applying the ADM: Applying Iteration to the ADM.
The Architecture Project encompasses management activities that can be grouped and sequenced as follows:

• Architecture Project start-up, which raises issues related to appointing the Executive and Project Manager, as well as the Project Management team, capturing previous lessons, selecting the project approach, assembling the project brief, and planning the following stage
• Architecture Project planning, which describes project scoping and planning activities based on Project Management methods
• Planning a stage, which describes how to split an Architecture Project into stages and plan a stage in alignment with an overall Project Plan
• Execute, monitor, and control a stage, which describes how to monitor and control architecture development activities of the ADM Phases B to F using Project Management methods
• Ending a stage, which describes key steps performed at a stage end

• Architecture Project closing (and handover of architecture deliverables for implementation), which describes the project closing activities and handover of the Architecture Project products to implementation programs and projects, and also the approach for documenting lessons learned

The above sequence forms an Architecture Project lifecycle, which is used as the basic structure to discuss Architecture Project Management in this document. This lifecycle maps into the TOGAF ADM (which describes architecture development phases and steps). It can be represented by Figure 2-2.
Figure 2-2: Architecture Project Lifecycle from the TOGAF ADM Perspective

Please note: to simplify it assumes Architecture Project is divided into stages that resemble the ADM phases (each stage covers one ADM phase). Usually, this is not the case – and in most cases should not be; the TOGAF Standard recommends an iterative approach, in which a stage can cover a few phases and can be executed repeatedly.

Dividing the Architecture Project into stages is discussed in detail in this document. For more information on the iterative approach to architecture development, refer to the TOGAF Standard — Applying the ADM: Applying Iteration to the ADM.

The Architecture Project lifecycle also maps to Project Management methods. Generally, these methods abstract from actual subject matter work in the project (i.e., architecture development), as they focus on management processes and steps needed for successful project execution.
Detailed mapping of the TOGAF ADM and most popular Project Management methods is presented in Chapter 4 and Chapter 5 of this document.

High-level mapping of the Architecture Project lifecycle to the TOGAF ADM phases and Project Management methods is presented in Table 2-2. Please note that the TOGAF Standard focuses on architecture development activities in the Architecture Project, and Project Management methods focus on managing successful execution of this endeavor.

To sum up, the Architecture Project lifecycle consists of six types of activities, which can be mapped to both the TOGAF ADM phases and Project Management method processes and steps. It is used to structure the detail presented in Chapter 3.

sections.translation_zh:
每种方法或框架都会定义自己的一套核心概念与定义。它们有时重叠；重叠概念的含义有时相近，有时并不相同——对于从一个专业领域转到另一个领域的人来说，这类词可称为“假朋友”（false friends）。

TOGAF 标准使用了 PRINCE2 与 PMBOK 定义的部分术语和概念，但若干关键定义的含义存在显著差异。表 2-3 列出从架构项目管理角度看至为关键的 TOGAF 与项目管理概念，讨论 TOGAF 标准、PRINCE2 与 PMBOK 中的定义，并说明本文档如何使用各术语。

**表 2-3：本文档涉及的 TOGAF 标准、PRINCE2 与 PMBOK 关键概念**

| 概念 | 讨论与定义 |
|---|---|
| 架构项目（Architecture Project） | 如本文档前文所述，架构项目是为定义并描述待实施的企业架构而开展的工作。按 TOGAF 术语，它涵盖 ADM 阶段 A 至 F 内的全部活动，以及这些阶段的需求管理。实践中它可以是独立项目，也可以是更大工作（如项目群）的一部分。TOGAF 标准未明确定义该术语，但框架中数处使用；项目管理方法中没有对应定义。 |
| 交付物（Deliverables） | 交付物是为完成项目或项目特定阶段而需要准备的、独特且可验证的产品、结果或输出。交付物可以是最终产品、辅助产品或项目管理产品的一部分。该术语在 TOGAF 标准（更具体，定义了更多特征、验收流程等）与项目管理方法（更通用）中含义相近，故以 TOGAF 定义为主，但项目管理方法的定义同样适用。TOGAF：“一种架构工作产品，通过合同规定，并由利益相关者正式评审、同意并签署。注：交付物代表项目的输出；以文档形式存在的交付物通常在项目完成时归档，或作为参考模型、标准或某一时点架构全景的快照转入架构库。” PRINCE2：与“输出（Output）”同义，即“移交给用户的专业产品”。PMBOK 第 5 版：“为完成某一过程、阶段或项目而必须产出的任何独特且可验证的产品、结果或提供服务的能力。” |
| 执行发起人（Executive） | 执行发起人是业务目标的所有者，负责预期收益的实现与项目的最终成功。其角色可与 PMBOK 的 Sponsor、TOGAF 标准的 Executive（在技能框架中可视为 Architecture Sponsor）相比，但 PMBOK 中 Sponsor 的参与程度更为有限。为清晰起见，本文档无论指哪种方法，均用“Executive（执行发起人）”表示这一使能角色。TOGAF：无明确定义，但把关键关注点表述为“按时、按预算交付变革举措，为组织实现预期收益”。PRINCE2：“对确保项目达成目标并交付预期收益负总体责任的单一个人。此人应确保项目保持业务聚焦、具有明确授权，并对工作（包括风险）进行积极管理。”PMBOK 第 5 版：（Sponsor）“为项目、项目群或项目组合提供资源与支持，并对促成其成功负责的个人或团体。” |
| 阶段（Phase） | 本文档用“phase（阶段）”指 TOGAF ADM 阶段，这与 PMBOK 通篇使用的“project phase”不同——对项目阶段本文档用“stage”（见下）。TOGAF：广泛用于描述 ADM 内被划分为若干指定阶段的逻辑相关工作集合，如阶段 A——架构愿景。PRINCE2：无特殊含义。PMBOK 第 5 版：“项目可划分为任意数量的阶段。项目阶段是一组逻辑相关的项目活动，以一个或多个交付物的完成告终。” |
| 项目经理（Project Manager） | 本文档用“项目经理”指负责确保项目（此处即架构项目）交付满足利益相关者需要的所需产品的人。这是两种项目管理方法定义的共同部分。TOGAF 标准未明确定义项目经理，故有必要沿用项目管理方法的术语。请注意，项目经理一职可由企业架构师或项目管理专业人士担任，详见 3.1.2 节。TOGAF：无特殊含义。PRINCE2：“被授予权责，在与项目委员会（Project Board）商定的约束内日常管理项目以交付所需产品的人。”PMBOK 第 5 版：“由执行组织指派、领导团队实现项目目标的个人。” |
| 风险（Risk） | 项目风险管理是项目管理的重要方面。按 PRINCE2 与 PMBOK，风险管理是项目经理必须具备能力的关键知识领域之一。PRINCE2 将项目风险定义为“一组一旦发生便会影响项目目标实现的事件”；PMBOK 定义为“一种不确定的事件或条件，一旦发生会对项目目标产生正面或负面影响”。须注意，风险对项目的影响可为负面（应采取的行动重在降低影响或发生概率），也可为正面（此时希望提高影响或发生概率）。风险与合规是任何业务活动或转型的固有部分，因此 TOGAF 标准要求在整个 ADM 中妥善考虑，详见架构能力框架。关键差异在于：TOGAF 标准把风险理解为转型对技术环境与合规的潜在威胁，而 PRINCE2 与 PMBOK 还把风险视为可能影响项目本身（进度、预算、质量等）的事件。 |
| 范围（Scope） | 本文档采用项目管理方法中的“scope（范围）”含义。它比 TOGAF ADM 阶段 A 中“定义范围（Define Scope）”步骤所述更宽，指为实现项目目标而要执行的工作范围；相比之下，TOGAF 标准把该词限定为待定义架构的范围。TOGAF：阶段 A 的定义范围步骤把范围限定为架构范围——“基线架构与目标架构工作范围内外的内容”。PRINCE2：“计划的范围是其产品的总和及其需求的程度，由该计划的产品分解结构及相关产品描述来表述。”PMBOK 第 5 版：“作为项目提供之产品、服务与结果的总和。” |
| 项目阶段（Stage） | 本文档用“stage（项目阶段）”指 PRINCE2 的 stage 或 PMBOK 的 project phase。本文档不使用“project phase”一词，以保留给 TOGAF ADM 阶段（见上）。TOGAF：无定义含义。PRINCE2：“项目的一个区段。”PMBOK 第 5 版：无定义含义。 |
| 利益相关者（Stakeholder） | 利益相关者在 TOGAF 标准与项目管理方法中的含义大体相同。作为架构生命周期标准，TOGAF 强调利益相关者关注架构的成果。TOGAF：“对系统有利益关系的个人、团队、组织或其类别。”PRINCE2：“能够影响、受其影响或自认为受某项举措（项目群、项目、活动、风险）影响的任何个人、群体或组织。”PMBOK 第 5 版：“可能影响、受其影响或自认为受项目决策、活动或结果影响的个人、群体或组织。” |
| 工作包（Work Package） | TOGAF 标准用该词描述将在企业中实施的变革举措，通常是较大的任务组（可能涵盖整个项目群）。项目管理方法用该词描述要执行的低层工作——需项目经理授权后团队才能开始的最细粒度工作。两者含义差别极大。本文档用“Project Work Package（项目工作包）”指项目任务（与 PRINCE2 用法及 PMBOK 定义一致），用“work package（工作包）”指架构项目识别的变革举措（与 TOGAF 定义一致）。TOGAF：“为实现一个或多个业务目标而识别的一组行动。工作包可以是项目的一部分、一个完整项目或一个项目群。”PRINCE2：“可预先描述、创建并测试的输入或输出，无论有形或无形。”PMBOK 第 5 版：“在工作分解结构最低层定义的工作，其成本与工期可估算并可管理。” |

（来源：改编自 TOGAF 标准、PRINCE2、PMBOK® 指南第 5 版）

本文档同时使用企业架构（TOGAF 标准）与项目管理（PRINCE2、PMBOK）两个学科的概念。由于本文档主要面向架构师，出现冲突时我们通常遵循 TOGAF 的定义。若读者背景不同，请留意表2-2（源文引用如此；概念定义表实际为表2-3）。

source_units.text_en: 2.3. Architecture Project Management Concepts

Every method or framework defines its own set of core concepts and definitions. Sometimes they overlap. Sometimes the meaning of overlapping concepts is similar, sometimes not – and they can be considered “false friends” for people who go from one subject matter world to another.

The TOGAF Standard uses some of the terms and concepts defined by PRINCE2 and PMBOK; however, there are significant differences in the meaning of some key definitions. Table 2-3 presents the TOGAF and Project Management concepts that are key from the perspective of Architecture Project Management. It discusses definitions presented in the TOGAF Standard, PRINCE2, and PMBOK, and presents how each term is used throughout this document.
Table 2-3: Key Concepts of the TOGAF Standard, PRINCE2, and PMBOK for this Document

| Concept | Discussion and Definitions | | --- | --- | | Architecture Project | As defined earlier in this document, an Architecture Project is an endeavor undertaken to define
and describe the Enterprise Architecture to be implemented. In TOGAF terms, it encompasses all
activities undertaken within the ADM Phases A to F, and Requirements Management for these
phases. Practically, it can be a stand-alone project or part of a larger effort (e.g., a program).
It has not been defined explicitly in the TOGAF Standard; however, it is used in the framework on
a few occasions.
There are no corresponding definitions for this concept in Project Management methods. | | Deliverables | Deliverables are unique and verifiable products, results, outputs that are required to be
prepared to complete the project or particular phase of the project. Deliverables may be part of
the final product, any auxiliary products, or Project Management products. This term is similar
in both the TOGAF Standard (where it is more specific, by defining more of the characteristics,
acceptance process, etc.) and Project Management methods (more generic), so the most
appropriate is the definition from the TOGAF Standard; however, the definitions from Project
Management methods are also applicable.
TOGAF Standard: “An architectural work product that is contractually specified and in turn
formally reviewed, agreed, and signed off by the stakeholders.
Note: Deliverables represent the output of projects and those deliverables that are in
documentation form will typically be archived at completion of a project, or transitioned into an
Architecture Repository as a reference model, standard, or snapshot of the Architecture
Landscape at a point in time.”
PRINCE2: Synonymous with “Output”, which is defined as: “A specialist product that is handed
over to a user(s)”.
PMBOK Guide, 5th Edition: “Any unique and verifiable product, result, or capability to perform
a service that is required to be produced to complete a process, phase, or project.” | | Executive | The Executive is the owner of the business goal, responsible for realization of expected benefits,
and ultimate success of the project. Its role is comparable with the roles of Sponsor and
Executive (which can be considered synonymous with Architecture Sponsor from the Skills
Framework) in PMBOK and the TOGAF Standard, respectively, though in the case of PMBOK the
involvement of the Sponsor versus Executive is more limited. For the sake of clarity, in this
document we will use “Executive” to define such enabling role, no matter what method we refer
to in a particular context.
TOGAF Standard: No explicitly stated definition, but has named key concerns as “On-time, on-
budget delivery of a change initiative that will realize expected benefits for the organization”.
PRINCE2: “The single individual with overall responsibility for ensuring that a project meets its
objectives and delivers the projected benefits. This individual should ensure that the project
maintains its business focus, that it has clear authority, and that the work, including risks, is
actively managed.”
PMBOK Guide, 5th Edition: (Sponsor) “A person or group who provides resources and support
for the project, program, or portfolio and is accountable for enabling success.” |

| Concept | Discussion and Definitions | | --- | --- | | Phase | In this document, we use the term “phase” for the TOGAF ADM phases. This is different from the
“project phase” term used throughout PMBOK – we use the term “stage” for project phases (see
Stage below).
TOGAF Standard: Used extensively to describe a collection of logically-related work within the
ADM, which is divided into specified phases; e.g., Phase A – Architecture Vision.
PRINCE2: No special meaning.
PMBOK Guide, 5th Edition: “A project may be divided into any number of phases. A project
phase is a collection of logically-related project activities that culminates in the completion of one
or more deliverables.” | | Project Manager | In this document, we use the term “Project Manager” to describe a person responsible for
ensuring that the project (in this case, Architecture Project) delivers the required product that
satisfies the stakeholders’ needs.
This constitutes the common part of the definitions from both Project Management methods. The
TOGAF Standard does not explicitly define Project Manager, so use of the term based on the
Project Management methods was necessary.
Please note that the role of Project Manager can be appointed to an Enterprise Architect or to a
Project Management professional; refer to Section 3.1.2 for details.
TOGAF Standard: No special meaning.
PRINCE2: “The person given the authority and responsibility to manage the project on a day-to-
day basis to deliver the required products within the constraints agreed with the Project Board.”
PMBOK Guide, 5th Edition: “The person assigned by the performing organization to lead the
team that is responsible for achieving the project objectives.” | | Risk | Project risk management is an important aspect of Project Management. According to the
PRINCE2 and PMBOK, risk management is one of the key knowledge areas in which a Project
Manager must be competent.
Project risk is defined by PRINCE2 as “a set of events that, should they occur, will have an effect
on achieving the project objectives” [PRINCE2] and by PMBOK as “an uncertain event or
condition that, if it occurs, has a positive or negative effect on a project’s objectives” [PMI].
It is important to note that risk impact on a project can be either negative (and actions taken
should be focused on minimizing the effect or probability of occurrence) or positive, when we
would like to increase the impact or probability of occurrence of such an event.
Risk and compliance are an inherent part of any business activity or transformation, thus the
TOGAF Standard requires proper consideration throughout the ADM, as defined in the
Architecture Capability Framework.
The key difference is that the TOGAF Standard understands risk as a potential threat of the
transformation to the technical environment and compliance, while PRINCE2 and PMBOK are
also considering risk as an event that can affect the project itself (timeline, budget, quality, etc.). |

| Concept | Discussion and Definitions | | --- | --- | | Scope | In this document, we use the term “scope: as defined in the Project Management methods. This is
a broader meaning than described in the Define Scope step of the TOGAF ADM Phase A, and it
means the scope of work that is to be performed in order to achieve projects goals. In contrast,
the TOGAF Standard restricts use of the term scope to the scope of the architecture to be defined.
TOGAF Standard: The Define Scope step of the ADM Phase A restricts the scope definition to the
scope of architecture: “what is inside and what is outside the scope of the Baseline Architecture
and Target Architecture efforts”.
PRINCE2: “The scope of a plan is the sum total of its products and the extent of their
requirements. It is described by the product breakdown structure for the plan and associated
product descriptions.”
PMBOK Guide, 5th Edition: “The sum of the products, services, and results to be provided as a
project.” | | Stage | In this document, we use the term “stage” for stages (as defined in PRINCE2) or project phases (as
defined in PMBOK). We do not use the term “project phase” as we reserve it for the TOGAF ADM
phases (see Phase above).
TOGAF Standard: No defined meaning.
PRINCE2: “A section of a project.”
PMBOK Guide, 5th Edition: No defined meaning. | | Stakeholder | The meaning of stakeholder in the TOGAF Standard and Project Management methods is
generally the same. The TOGAF Standard, as an architecture lifecycle standard, highlights that
the stakeholder focuses on the outcomes of the architecture.
TOGAF Standard: “An individual, team, organization, or class thereof, having an interest in a
system”; see the TOGAF Standard — Introduction and Core Concepts: Definitions (Stakeholder).
PRINCE2: “Any individual, group, or organization that can affect, be affected by, or perceive
itself to be affected by, an initiative (program, project, activity, risk)” [PRINCE2].
PMBOK Guide, 5th Edition: “An individual, group, or organization who may affect, be affected
by, or perceive itself to be affected by a decision, activity, or outcome of a project” [PMBOK]. |

| Concept | Discussion and Definitions | | --- | --- | | Work Package | The TOGAF Standard uses the term work package to describe change initiatives that will be
implemented in the enterprise. These initiatives are typically large groups of tasks (i.e., they may
encompass a whole program).
Project Management methods use the term work package to describe a low-level part of work to
be performed – the most granular part of work that needs the Project Manager’s authorization
before it is started by the team.
The two meanings are vastly different. In this document, we use the term “Project Work
Package” for project tasks (in line with the PRINCE2 use of the term and the PMBOK definition
below) and “work package” for change initiatives identified by Architecture Projects (in line with
the TOGAF definition below).
TOGAF Standard: “A set of actions identified to achieve one or more objectives for the business.
A work package can be a part of a project, a complete project, or a program.”
PRINCE2: “An input or output, whether tangible or intangible, that can be described in advance,
created, and tested.”
PMBOK Guide, 5th Edition: “The work defined at the lowest level of the work breakdown
structure for which cost and duration can be estimated and managed.” |
(Source: Derived from the TOGAF Standard, PRINCE2, PMBOK Guide, 5th Edition)

In this document we use concepts from both Enterprise Architecture (TOGAF Standard) and Project Management (PRINCE2, PMBOK) disciplines. As this document is addressed primarily to architects, in case of conflicts, we usually stick to the TOGAF definitions. If you have a different background, please keep Table 2-2 in mind.

项目管理的本质是沟通。项目经理负责向项目利益相关者——项目发起人（Project Sponsor）、指导委员会（Steering Committee）及其他利益相关者——沟通项目计划、状态与风险。这可以正式或非正式地进行，形式多样，例如电话、会议、演示或书面报告，具体取决于项目规模、组织文化与利益相关者要求等因素。

本文档经常提到可以或应当形成文档的计划、报告及其他制品。这并不意味着每件制品都要成为独立文档。在较小的项目与更敏捷的组织中，可能几乎不需要文档。不过，我们仍建议把项目管理制品以书面形式记录下来，哪怕只是一封电子邮件——这样可以回溯计划、重要决策与项目里程碑；如有必要，还可在此基础上编制更正式的文档。

[1] 关于架构层级，参见TOGAF标准——应用ADM：跨架构全景应用ADM。

[2] 关于架构域，参见TOGAF标准——应用ADM：核心概念（TOGAF标准涉及哪种架构？）。

source_units.text_en: 2.4. Project Management Documentation

Project Management is about communication. The Project Manager is responsible for communicating project plans, statuses, and risks to project stakeholders — the Project Sponsor, Steering Committee, and other stakeholders. This can be effectively achieved formally or informally, and in many forms – such as phone calls, meetings, presentations, or written reports. It depends on project size, organizational culture, and stakeholder requirements among other things.

In this document, we often refer to plans, reports, and other artifacts that can or should be documented. This does not mean every such artifact should be a separate document. In smaller projects and more Agile organizations, very little documentation may be required or necessary. However, we do recommend that Project Management artifacts are documented in a written form, even as simple as email. This allows for tracing back plans, important decisions, and project milestones. In addition, documentation that is more formal can be prepared based on it, if necessary.
Endnotes
[1] For guidance on architecture levels, refer to the TOGAF Standard — Applying the ADM: Applying the ADM Across the Architecture Landscape.
[2] For guidance on architecture domains, refer to the TOGAF Standard — Applying the ADM: Core Concepts (What Kind of Architecture Does the TOGAF Standard Deal With?).

本章描述开发企业架构时可用的详细项目管理方法。本章读者为已熟悉 TOGAF 标准并领导架构项目的企业架构师。

本章各小节分别描述以下工作的方法：

- **架构项目启动**：包含 ADM 阶段 A 的项目管理活动，以及项目管理方法的项目启动与“发起（Initiation）”活动；
- **架构项目规划**：包含基于项目管理方法的项目规划活动；
- **阶段规划**：描述如何运用项目管理方法规划架构项目的一个阶段；
- **执行、监控与控制阶段**：描述如何运用项目管理方法监控与控制 ADM 阶段 B–F 的架构开发活动；
- **阶段收尾**：描述在架构项目阶段结束时如何运用项目管理方法；
- **架构项目收尾**：包含项目管理方法的项目收尾活动与 ADM 阶段 F，包括把架构交付物移交给实施。






图3-1：本节结构及架构项目流（箭头）。

在适当之处，本指南引用一个或多个真实示例，以灰底框呈现，取自表 2-1 的示例项目清单。

> 本文档的方法覆盖了架构项目的大部分项目管理职责；但有些领域——如进度管理、采购管理、成本管理等——并未覆盖。我们假定本文档的目的不是完整讲解项目管理方法，而是就如何在架构项目的现实与特点中应用这些方法提供指导。由于采购、成本等领域与其他项目并无不同，本文档不予详述。

source_units.text_en: 3. Detailed Guidance

This section describes a detailed Project Management approach to use when developing Enterprise Architecture. The target audience of this section is Enterprise Architects who are already familiar with the TOGAF Standard [C220] and who lead Architecture Projects.
This section is organized into subsections which describe the approach to:
• Architecture Project start-up, which includes the Project Management activities of the ADM Phase A and the project start-up and “Initiation” activities of the Project Management methods
• Architecture Project planning, which includes project planning activities based on the Project Management methods
• Planning a stage, which describes how to apply the Project Management methods to plan an Architecture Project stage
• Execute, monitor, and control a stage, which describes how to monitor and control the architecture development activities of the ADM Phases B to F using the Project Management methods
• Ending a stage, which describes how to apply the Project Management methods at the end of an Architecture Project stage
• Architecture Project closing, which includes project closing activities of the Project Management methods and the ADM Phase F, including handover of architecture deliverables for implementation
Figure 3-1: Structure of this Section and Architecture Project Flow (arrows)
Where appropriate, guidance refers to one or more real-world examples. These examples are presented in gray boxes. They refer to selected projects from our examples list (see Table 2-1).

The approach in this document covers most of the Project Management responsibilities related to an Architecture Project; however, some areas — such as schedule management, procurement management, cost management, and others — are not covered. We assumed that the purpose of this document is not to explain the Project Management methods in full detail, but to provide guidance on how to apply them in the reality and characteristics of Architecture Projects. Since areas related to procurement, cost, etc. are not different from other projects, they are not detailed in this document.

sections.translation_zh:
ADM 周期阶段A的第一步在 TOGAF 标准“阶段 A：建立架构项目”中定义。该章非常简洁，把读者引向其他资料，指出“ADM 周期的执行应在企业的项目管理框架内进行”。它未详述架构项目最开始应执行的步骤，而是留给项目经理与企业内其他机构，依据其经验与一套组织标准决定要做哪些工作。

按第 4 章，ADM 步骤“建立架构项目”可映射到 PRINCE2 的“项目启动（Starting up a Project）”流程。PMBOK 因其性质不同，未提供如此详尽的系统性流程，但其“制定项目章程（Develop Project Charter）”流程同样可映射到该 TOGAF 步骤（见第 5 章）。

因此，启动项目需要以下活动：

- 任命执行发起人与项目经理
- 汲取以往经验（Capture Previous Lessons）
- 编制概要商业论证（Outline Business Case）
- 选择项目方法（Select the Project Approach）
- 设计并任命项目管理团队
- 汇编项目任务书（Project Brief）
- 定义管理方法（Define the Management Approach）

上述活动构成本章以下各小节的基础。

source_units.text_en: 3.1. Architecture Project Start-Up

The first step of Phase A of the ADM cycle is defined in the TOGAF Standard, Phase A: Establish the Architecture Project. The chapter is very concise and refers the reader to other sources, by stating: “execution of ADM cycles should be conducted within the Project Management framework of the enterprise”. It does not detail steps to be undertaken at the very beginning of the Architecture Project, but leaves it to the Project Manager and other bodies within the enterprise to decide on what has to be done based on their experience and a set of organizational standards.

According to Chapter 4, the ADM step Establish the Architecture Project can be mapped to the PRINCE2 Starting up a Project process [PRINCE2]. PMBOK [PMBOK], due to its different nature, does not provide such elaborate systematic processes, nevertheless its Develop Project Charter process can be mapped to this TOGAF step as well (see Chapter 5).
Therefore, the following activities are necessary for starting up a project:
• Appoint the Executive and Project Manager
• Capture Previous Lessons
• Prepare Outline Business Case
• Select the Project Approach
• Design and Appoint the Project Management Team
• Assemble the Project Brief
• Define the Management Approach
The above-mentioned activities form a basis for the following subsections.

sections.translation_zh:
项目应是对已识别业务需要的响应，因为其执行与组织有形且通常可量化的成本相关，例如现金支出、员工工时，甚至正常运营的中断。只有在提供必要资源时项目才能执行，而提供资源通常以项目将实现某种业务目标并带来充分回报（如业务收益、维持运营的能力等）为假设。

执行发起人是项目业务目标的所有者，因而是组织对该举措支持的化身，负责预期收益的实现。视组织（尤其是其项目管理框架）与项目本身（类型）不同，执行发起人可有不同名称与结构。该术语最初取自 PRINCE2 方法，在那里它是代表“客户（Customer）”的角色名称，客户是项目的最终资源提供者[1]。PMBOK 中的“Sponsor（发起人）”扮演非常相似但更受限的角色。TOGAF 标准亦然：执行发起人负责确保“按时、按预算交付变革举措，为组织实现预期收益”；参见 TOGAF 标准——ADM 技术：利益相关者管理（模板利益相关者图）。

TOGAF 标准未对执行发起人着墨太多。它把其列为一种利益相关者组织角色，可由发起人或项目群经理等担任；在技能框架中定义了所需技能（见 TOGAF® 系列指南：架构技能框架 [G198]（目标/理由））；说明了初始企业架构工作的赞助情况（通常由 CIO 或其他高管赞助），列出了架构的赞助者（架构委员会），以及“赞助者的赞助者”（公司最高层的执行赞助人）。

如前所述，没有执行发起人就没有项目：执行发起人提供项目执行所需的资源，并代表需要被满足的业务需要。执行发起人任命项目经理，并在运营层面把架构项目的执行任务交给项目经理。

> **示例 3-1**
>
> 架构项目可能带来多种收益，例如：
>
> - 更高效的运营
> - 现有投资获得更好的回报
> - 降低未来投资的风险
> - 更快、更简单、更便宜的采购
> - 通过设计新的业务模式、识别新的业务线，提高应对情境分析中所识别的威胁与机会以及竞争对手压力的能力
> - 通过不同渠道改善客户体验
>
> 这些都源于拥有良好、经过周密规划的企业架构（或至少得益于它），或源于开展架构工作。在其他情况下，架构项目是其他举措、项目与项目群的使能者，本身并不直接交付价值，或者只是必然地以外部因素（如满足监管合规要求）为依据。

> **示例 3-2**
>
> | 总体目标 | 架构项目目标 | 架构项目执行发起人 |
> |---|---|---|
> | （B）改进物流流程效率、缩短订单周期 | 确定并设计物流领域业务流程的可能改进 | CIO |
> | （E）实施新的数据仓库与管理信息系统，以满足不断扩大的银行报告需求 | 使该解决方案能够高效、成功地实施 | 项目群经理，负责管理信息系统转型项目群 |

source_units.text_en: 3.1.1. Appoint the Executive

The project should be a response to an identified business need, as its execution is connected with tangible and usually quantifiable costs for the organization, in the form of, for example, cash expenditure, man-hours of employees, and even disruptions in normal operations. The project can only be executed when there are necessary resources provided, usually on the assumption that they will achieve some business goal and provide sufficient return in some form (like business benefits, ability to continue operations, etc.).
Example 3-1
There are multiple possible benefits of Architecture Projects; for example:
• A more efficient operation
• Better return on existing investment
• Reduced risk for future investment
• Faster, simpler, and cheaper procurement

• Improved ability to respond to threats and opportunities identified from a context analysis, as well as competitor pressure, through design of new business models and identification of new business lines
• Improved customer experience through different channels

which all stem from having good, thoroughly planned Enterprise Architecture (or, at the very least, are facilitated by it) or undertaking architectural efforts. In other cases, Architecture Projects are enablers of other initiatives, projects, and programs, and do not deliver value on their own, or are just necessarily grounded in external factors (like compliance with regulatory requirements).

The Executive is the owner of the project’s business goal, and therefore an incarnation of organizational support for the initiative at hand, responsible for realization of expected benefits. Depending on the organization (especially its Project Management framework) and the project itself (its type), the Executive can have different names and structures. The term was originally taken from the PRINCE2 method, where it is the name of the role representing the “Customer”, who is the ultimate resource provider for the project.[1] A very similar role, though more limited, is played by the “Sponsor” in PMBOK. The same is the case with the TOGAF Standard, where the Executive is responsible for ensuring “on-time, on-budget delivery of a change initiative that will realize expected benefits for the organization”; see the TOGAF Standard — ADM Techniques: Stakeholder Management (Template Stakeholder Map).

The TOGAF Standard does not elaborate on the Executive much. It is named as a stakeholder organizational role, which can be played by, for example, a sponsor or program manager. It defines the necessary skill set (see the TOGAF® Series Guide: Architecture Skills Framework [G198] (Goals/Rationale)) in the skills framework, provides information on the sponsorship of the initial Enterprise Architecture effort (namely that it is usually a CIO or other Executive), names the sponsor of the architecture (Architecture Board), as well as the “sponsor of sponsors” (Executive sponsor from the highest level of the corporation).

As pointed out earlier, there can be no project without an Executive, who provides the necessary resources for the project’s execution and represents the need to be addressed. The Executive is the person that appoints the Project Manager and tasks them with Architecture Project execution at the operational level.
Example 3-2

efficiency and shorten time-to-order | Determine and design possible
improvements in the business
processes in the area of logistics | CIO |

| | Overall Goal | Architecture Project Goal | Architecture Project Executive | | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | | (E) Implement new data warehouse
and management information

sections.translation_zh:
如上述“任命执行发起人”步骤所述，项目经理由执行发起人任命，在运营层面领导架构项目。

项目经理是负责确保项目交付满足利益相关者需要的所需产品的人。因此，项目经理必须具备很强的领导、沟通与谈判能力，才能引领利益相关者走向项目成功的结果。

按 PRINCE2，项目经理是被授予权责、日常管理项目以在与项目委员会商定的约束内交付所需产品的人。项目经理的首要职责是确保项目在规定的时间、成本、质量、范围、风险与收益容差内产出所需产品；同时负责使项目交付能够实现商业论证所述收益的结果 [PRINCE2, §C.5（Project Manager）]。

按 PMBOK，项目经理是由执行组织指派、领导团队实现项目目标的个人。一般而言，项目经理有责任满足任务需要、团队需要与个人需要 [PMBOK, §1.7（Role of the Project Manager）]。

一个常见问题是：谁应担任架构项目的项目经理？项目管理方法主张把这一角色交给项目管理专业人士。

TOGAF 标准未回答该问题，但 TOGAF® 系列指南：架构技能框架 [G198] 对交付成功企业架构所需技能给出了评估。按该框架，企业架构师负责确保架构的完备性（completeness，即适用性 fitness-for-purpose），充分覆盖利益相关者所有相关关注点；以及架构的统合性（integrity），即把各种视图相互连接、令人满意地调和不同利益相关者的冲突关注点，并展示所作权衡。因此，对多数架构项目而言，企业架构师一职即满足项目经理的定义。此外，企业架构师所需的与利益相关者的出色沟通能力，降低了对 IT 项目通常所需的专职项目经理的需求。

但在某些情况下，可能需要把架构项目的管理与控制委托给专职项目经理。是否在架构项目中设置专职项目经理，取决于组织采用的项目管理规则与原则、架构项目的规模、所涉内部单位与外部供应商的数量、项目工作流的数量及其时间框架等。你可能会发现架构项目过于复杂，以致企业架构师与项目经理的角色合并后不再有效——因为按组织项目管理规则管理与控制项目的工作量，会限制企业架构师专注于核心架构工作。

本文档余下部分用“项目经理”指负责架构项目执行的角色。如上所述，该角色可由企业架构师或项目管理专业人士担任。

> **示例 3-3**
>
> 在项目 B 中，由一名企业架构师担任项目经理。这之所以可行，是因为项目复杂度较低——它只覆盖一个业务域，涉及来自三个业务单元的人员和五到十个 IT 系统。此外，组织采用的项目管理规则与原则只关注报告与在既定时间与成本容差内交付项目相关的问题与风险。
>
> 在项目 D 中，由于项目复杂，需要设置专职项目经理——该项目由五个工作流组成（架构是其中之一），各工作流的产品相互依赖，覆盖 25 个以上 IT 系统，涉及来自不同业务单元的 50 多人。企业架构师负责管理架构工作流中的工作，并向项目经理报告其状态；项目经理的职责之一，是汇总所有工作流的状态报告，并每周向利益相关者呈报项目总体状态。

source_units.text_en: 3.1.2. Appoint the Project Manager
As stated in the Appoint the Executive step above, the Project Manager is appointed by the Executive to lead the Architecture Project on the operational level.

A Project Manager is a person responsible for ensuring that the project delivers the required product that satisfies the stakeholders’ needs. Therefore, a Project Manager must have strong leadership, communication, and negotiation skills in order to lead the stakeholders to the project’s successful outcome.

According to PRINCE2, the Project Manager is a person given the authority and responsibility to manage the project on a day-to-day basis to deliver the required products with the constraints agreed with the Project Board. The Project Manager’s prime responsibility is to ensure that the project produces the required products within the specified tolerances of time, cost, quality, scope, risk, and benefits. The Project Manager is also responsible for the project delivering a result capable of achieving the benefits defined in the business case [PRINCE2, §C.5 (Project Manager)].

According to PMBOK, the Project Manager is a person assigned by the performing organization to lead the team that is responsible for achieving the project objectives. In general, Project Managers have the responsibility to satisfy the needs: task needs, team needs, and individual needs [PMBOK, §1.7 (Role of the Project Manager)].
A common question is: who should be an Architecture Project Manager? Project Management methods advocate assigning such a role to a Project Management professional.

The TOGAF Standard does not answer this question, but the TOGAF® Series Guide: Architecture Skills Framework[G198] provides an assessment of the skills required to deliver a successful Enterprise Architecture. According to the framework, the Enterprise Architect is responsible for ensuring the completeness (fitness-for-purpose) of the architecture, in terms of adequately addressing all the pertinent concerns of its stakeholders; and the integrity of the architecture, in terms of connecting all the various views to each other, satisfactorily reconciling the conflicting concerns of different stakeholders, and showing the trade-offs made. Therefore, for most Architecture Projects, the role of an Enterprise Architect satisfies the definition of the Project Manager. In addition, excellent communication with stakeholders required from the Enterprise Architect lowers the need to designate a dedicated Project Manager that is typical for IT projects.

However, in some cases there may be a need to delegate Architecture Project Management and control to a dedicated Project Manager. The decision to include a dedicated Project Manager in an Architecture Project will depend on the Project Management rules and principles adopted in the organization, the scale of the Architecture Project, the number of internal entities and external suppliers involved in the

project, the number of project streams, its timeframe, etc. You may find that the Architecture Project is so complex that combining an Enterprise Architect role with the Project Manager role may not be effective because the workload connected with managing and controlling the project according to the organization’s Project Management rules and principles limits the Enterprise Architect to focus on core architecture work.
Example 3-3

In Project B, an Enterprise Architect served as a Project Manager. This was possible due to the low complexity of the project — it covered only one business domain, engaged people from three business units, and five to ten IT systems. Moreover, the Project Management rules and principles adopted in the organization were focused only on reporting issues and risks associated with delivering the project within the specified tolerances of time and cost.

In Project D, there was a need to include a dedicated Project Manager due to the complexity of the project — it consisted of five work streams (architecture was one of them) whose products were inter-dependent, covered over 25 IT systems, and engaged over 50 people from various business units. The Enterprise Architect was responsible for managing the work in the architecture stream and reporting its status to the Project Manager who was, among others, responsible for consolidating status reports from all streams and presenting an overall status of the project to its stakeholders on a weekly basis.

In the rest of this document, we use “Project Manager” for a role responsible for the execution of the Architecture Project. This role can be assigned to an Enterprise Architect or to a Project Management professional, as discussed above.

sections.translation_zh:
按 PRINCE2 方法，项目经理获任命后首先要做的事情之一，是编制经验记录（Lessons Log）[2]。该文档应作为当前项目知识的非正式仓库。项目伊始，就应填入有关类似项目的全部可得相关信息，包括以往项目经验记录（或经验报告，如有）中的关键信息、其他相关文档、参与此类工作的人的经验，以及一切其他潜在知识来源（对架构项目而言，输入还应包括阶段 F 所记录的经验教训[3]）。这使项目经理能更好地洞察项目性质，并通过避免他人已犯的错误、利用已积累的专有知识，更好地准备与执行项目。

该文档应定期更新，补充新获得的信息以及形成的良好实践与最佳实践，以支持项目经理在本项目及其他项目中的工作。

该文档的详细程度应与项目要求（规模与复杂度）相称，并符合特定组织的内部规定。小型项目无需编制复杂的经验记录；某些情况下，一份包含最重要观察的要点清单即可。

> **示例 3-4**
>
> 项目经理受命管理一个聚焦于新数据仓库与管理信息系统（项目 E）架构设计与实施的项目。作为第一步，项目经理收集了有关当前项目的信息，并访谈了发起人。
>
> 为确保潜在有用信息的完整性、完备性与持续可用性，他建立了经验记录（Lessons Log），打算一开始把所有他认为有用的信息放进去，并在项目执行期间把获得的所有洞见补充进去。结果发现，公司里还有另一个项目，其范围与预算与当前项目相似，但因未能在估算时间内完成而以失败告终。记录在案的原因是：让主要架构师承担项目管理职责，而在这类项目类型与组织安排下，这对一个人来说负担过重。项目经理在经验记录中写下这样一条：“在此类范围的项目中，项目管理与企业架构职责应分开；否则，由于工作量过大，这两项职能都有无法妥善执行的风险。”

source_units.text_en: 3.1.3. Capture Previous Lessons

One of the first things the Project Manager is expected to do after being appointed, as per the PRINCE2 method, is preparation of a Lessons Log.[2] This document should function as an informal repository of knowledge about the current project. At the very beginning, it should be completed with all relevant information available about similar projects, including key information from previous projects’ Lessons Logs (or Lessons Reports, if these exist) and other relevant documentation, experiences of people involved in such endeavors, and all other potential sources of knowledge (in case of Architecture Projects, the input should be obtained, among other sources, from the lessons learned documented in Phase F.[3]) It enables the Project Manager to gain better insight into the nature of the project and better prepare and execute the project by avoiding mistakes made previously by others and using developed know-how.

The document should undergo regular updates when it should be filled in with additional information acquired as well as developed good and best practices, which will support the Project Manager in his duties on this and other projects.

The level of detail in this document should be adequate to the requirements of the project (its scale and complexity) and compliant with the internal regulations of the particular organization. There is no
need to create sophisticated Lessons Logs for small projects. In some cases even a bullet list, containing the most important observations, might be sufficient.
Example 3-4

The Project Manager has been appointed to manage the project focusing on the architecture design and implementation of a new Data Warehouse and Management Information System (Project E). As a first step, the Project Manager gathered information about the project at hand and interviewed the Sponsor.

In order to ensure integrity, completeness, and constant availability of potentially useful information, he created the Lessons Log, where he intended to put all the information he considered useful at the beginning, and where he will include all the insights gained during the project execution. As it turned out, there was another project executed in the company, which resembled the current project in scope and budget and ended in failure due to not being completed in the estimated time. The documented reason for that was tasking the main architect with Project Management duties, which proved to be too much to handle for one person in this project type and set-up. The Project Manager included the note in the Lessons Log: “In projects with such scope, the Project Management and Enterprise Architecture duties should be separated; otherwise, there is a risk of neither of these functions being executed properly due to the excessive workload.”

sections.translation_zh:
同时，PRINCE2 方法要求编制概要商业论证，它将成为项目任务书的组成部分，提供项目预期成本、风险与收益的信息。概要商业论证试图对项目作定量与定性评估，使决策者（执行发起人或类似机构）能够更知情地判断项目是否可行且有益，以及在全部项目构想组合中它是否最值得开展。

该文档由执行发起人负责，但这不意味着必须由其亲自编制，该任务可委托给业务分析师或项目经理等。

随着后续规划工作的开展，该文档应逐步细化，并应定期核实、持续维护，以提供关于可能影响项目结果的各种因素的最新认识。它构成关于项目的战略决策的基础，包括判断继续进行中的项目是否仍然有益、可行且必要（见 3.4 节）。项目完成后还应确认商业论证，检验关于收益的预测是否正确（见 3.6 节）。

> **示例 3-5**
>
> 项目经理受命为项目 C（整合近期合并企业的 IT 环境）编制商业论证。新建的 IT 环境在很大程度上是冗余的，通过应用与基础设施整合可显著降低 IT 成本。预计每年可节省 2000 万至 5000 万欧元。用于定义目标模型与整合路线图的架构项目，估计需要企业架构师4个全职当量（FTE）及其他人员8个全职当量，投入六个月（总成本 50 万欧元，含预期风险实际发生的成本）。路线图实施预计耗资 4000 万至 1 亿欧元。
>
> 项目经理把这些初步结论记录在概要商业论证中，并告知执行发起人，同时说明这些结论还需进一步分析；但他认为项目看起来很有前景，应当继续——至少应继续到能够基于架构项目成果编制更精确的成本效益分析之时。

source_units.text_en: 3.1.4. Prepare Outline Business Case

Simultaneously, the PRINCE2 method expects the preparation of an outline business case, which will be an integral part of the Project Brief, providing information on expected costs, risks, and benefits of the project. The outline business case is an attempt at providing quantitative and qualitative assessment of the project, enabling the decision-makers (i.e., the Executive or similar body) to make a more informed choice about whether the project is feasible and beneficial, and whether it is the best project to undertake from the whole portfolio of project ideas.
The document is a responsibility of the Executive, though it does not mean that they prepare it. This task might be delegated to, for example, business analysts or the Project Manager.

This document should become more detailed later on, as additional planning efforts are conducted, and should be regularly verified and continuously maintained to provide the current state of knowledge about all factors that might affect the outcome of the project. This constitutes a basis for strategic decisions regarding the project, including a decision on whether the continuing project is still beneficial, feasible, and needed (see Section 3.4). After the completion of the project, the business case should also be confirmed, to see whether the forecasts regarding benefits were correct (see Section 3.6).
Example 3-5

The Project Manager has been tasked with creating the business case for Project C (Consolidate IT environment of recently merged businesses). The newly created IT environment is largely redundant, allowing for a significant reduction of IT costs through application and infrastructure consolidation. Possible savings are estimated at 20-50M EUR yearly. The Architecture Project that will define the target model and consolidation roadmap is estimated to involve four FTE of Enterprise Architects and eight FTE of other staff for six months (total cost of 0.5M EUR including expected risk materialization costs). The resulting roadmap implementation is estimated to cost between 40M and 100M EUR.

The Project Manager has documented these preliminary findings in an outline business case and communicated them to the Executive, mentioning that these require further analysis, but the project looks promising and should be, in his opinion, continued, at least until a more precise cost benefit analysis can be prepared based on Architecture Project findings.

sections.translation_zh:
PRINCE2 期望项目经理选择项目执行的方法。PRINCE2 方法提及的决策包括：使用何种资源（内部或外部）、是从零构建解决方案还是修改现有方案、是基于商用现货（COTS）方案还是定制开发。

对架构项目而言，只有第一项决策直接相关。但从架构项目管理的角度看，“方法”应作更宽的理解：用什么方法与框架管理架构项目，以及如何规划项目。

架构项目管理所用方法与框架的选择，应源于项目所要解决问题的特征，并与所采用的规划方式相联系。由于架构项目管理是项目管理与企业架构两个领域的复合，应分别就这两个领域所用的工具作出决策。

**1. 选择所用资源**

根据我们的经验，决定使用内部还是外部资源时，至少应考虑：

- 项目的估计复杂度与所需工作量；
- 时间与预算约束；
- 所需技能——注意，对现有架构的了解可能高度相关；若使用外部顾问，应仔细考虑获取这些知识（即现状分析）的成本；
- 组织内部可用的资源；
- 以往经验与组织导则。

> **示例 3-6**
>
> 负责管理项目 E 的项目经理得出结论：由于估计范围广、复杂度高、难度大，加之银行法定义务带来的严格时间约束，项目需要多名在数据域具有高能力的架构师。现有资源经评估不足，既无法及时招聘更多人员，也无法把现有架构师培训到足够技能水平。
>
> 项目经理决定采用外部资源开展项目，聘请某咨询公司的一组架构师；该银行与该咨询公司有长期、良好的合作关系，并曾成功完成其他项目。

**2. 选择规划方式**

规划方式与方法/框架的决策相互依存，彼此影响。TOGAF 标准倡导迭代方式，反复迭代直至产品达到预期的质量与一致性——许多人把这与敏捷方式和方法等同起来。事实并非如此：所建议的方式与瀑布方法之间并无根本矛盾。不过，这可能需要裁剪 TOGAF 框架，以适配项目管理方法与具体项目的约束。关于如何规划项目、特别是如何把项目划分为阶段，参见 3.2 节与 3.3 节。

**3. 选择方法**

在选择针对特定问题的最佳途径（从项目管理方法角度看）时，Cynefin 框架可能有用。它把所谓问题域分为四大类：复杂（complex）、繁杂（complicated）、明显/简单（obvious/simple）与混乱（chaotic）[4]。依问题类别不同，推荐的方法也不同，因为各方法在不同情形下各有优势与不足。根据我们的经验，对各问题类别推荐如下：

- **复杂**——SCRUM 方法，专为应对高度易变与不确定性而设计；
- **繁杂**——如看板（Kanban）与 SCRUM 方法，因为该类别涵盖需要仔细分析、高度专家知识才能解决，且因不存在唯一最优解而需一定探索的问题；
- **明显（简单）**——各类瀑布方法，因为该类别涵盖已知问题且已有最佳实践，可采用精心预先规划的方式；
- **混乱**——不推荐任何方法，因为系统行为完全不可预测。

企业架构领域的问题往往符合简单与繁杂类别的判据，尤其在组织已有架构时，因为其目标是提高秩序与可预测性。因果关系存在且可辨识；问题可能变为复杂或混乱的唯一情形，是环境高度易变（通常还伴随对本组织及其外部环境缺乏了解）。特定问题属于哪个域，取决于组织的专业能力、架构成熟度、项目范围以及所受的额外约束等。判定问题类别是项目经理的任务。

**4. 选择企业架构框架**

在企业架构领域，需在不同架构框架之间作出选择。至少有几个主要框架为企业架构师提供工具与资源（包括 Zachman 企业架构框架™ 与联邦企业架构（FEA））。但并非所有框架都适用于架构项目管理，这是各框架关注点不同所致。由于架构项目管理实际上是创建架构的过程，只应考虑那些提供架构创建方法的框架。在这方面，TOGAF 框架凭借对 ADM 的详细描述而优于其他框架。

> **示例 3-7**
>
> 在项目 A 中，项目经理并不清楚实现项目目标需要哪些视图，这使其成为一个繁杂（complicated）问题。因此他决定在开始时设置一个“概览”阶段，以便确定范围，从而使项目能在既定时间框架与既定资源下完成。在该阶段对两个应用作了深入分析之后，他与执行发起人确认了后续阶段可做哪些工作，并将满足执行发起人现有的业务需要。此后，项目经理决定采用迭代方式，把所使用的 50 个应用分成每组八个，在每两周一次的迭代中评估一组。
>
> 在项目 E 中，项目经理必须在确定日期交付精确描述的制品与产品；在具备必要资源的前提下，这使其成为一个简单问题。若未能做到，将导致项目出现代价高昂的延误，包括因未满足监管要求而被罚款，因为架构工作流处于关键路径上。因此，项目经理采用了预先规划的方式，设置带缓冲的时间限定阶段，并最初聚焦于基线（基线优先方式）。该计划已被参与项目的外部咨询专家评估为可行，这些专家过去参与过类似项目。尽管如此，风险仍被评估并沟通，其重要部分通过合同中的附加条款转移给了咨询公司。

本文档假定架构项目按 TOGAF 框架开展，并辅以源自最流行项目管理方法的实践。

source_units.text_en: 3.1.5. Select the Project Approach

PRINCE2 expects the Project Manager to select the approach to project execution. Decisions to be made mentioned by the PRINCE2 method are, among others: what resources to use (internal or external), whether to build a solution from scratch or modify existing solutions, or whether to base it on a Commercial Off-The-Shelf (COTS) solution, or create a tailor-made one.

In the case of Architecture Projects, only the first decision is relevant. However, from the perspective of Architecture Project Management, the approach should be understood more broadly: what methods and frameworks should be used to manage the Architecture Project and how to plan the project.

The choice of methods and frameworks used in the Architecture Project Management should stem from the characteristics of the problem the project aims to solve and be connected with the adopted planning approach. Since the area of Architecture Project Management is a composite of Project Management and Enterprise Architecture fields, decisions should be made regarding tools used in each of these domains.
1. Choosing the Resources to Use
From our experience, the decision on whether to use internal or external resources should be made taking into consideration at least the following:
• Estimated complexity of the project and amount of work needed
• Time and budget constraints

• Necessary skills — note that knowledge of the existing architecture may be highly relevant; cost of obtaining it (i.e., current state analysis) should be carefully considered for external consultants
• Available resources inside the organization
• Previous experiences and organizational guidelines
Example 3-6

The Project Manager tasked with managing Project E has concluded that due to broad estimated scope, high complexity, and difficulty of the project, as well as strict time constraints resulting from legal obligations of the bank, the project requires multiple architects with high competency in the data domain. The resources at hand were assessed as insufficient and there was neither possibility to recruit more people in time, nor to train the available architects to the adequate skill level.

The Project Manager has decided to approach the project using external resources by engaging a group of architects from the consulting firm, with which the bank has a longstanding, positive relationship and has successfully completed other projects.
2. Choosing a Planning Approach

The decisions regarding planning approach and methods/frameworks are inter-dependent, as each may influence the other. The TOGAF Standard advocates an iterative approach with iterations repeated until the product achieves the expected quality and consistency, which many people equate with the Agile approach and methods. This is not the case, and there is no fundamental contradiction between the proposed approach and the waterfall methods. Nevertheless, it might require tailoring of the TOGAF Framework to fit within the constraints of the Project Management methods and particular projects. For more information on how to plan the project, with particular focus on dividing it into stages, refer to Section 3.2 and Section 3.3.
3. Choosing a Method

Useful in the case of choosing the best approach (from the Project Management method viewpoint) to the particular problem could be the Cynefin Framework. It divides the so-called problem domain into four main categories: complex, complicated, obvious (simple), and chaotic.[4] Depending on the category of the problem, different methods are recommended, due to them being best suited for different circumstances as they have different strengths and weaknesses. In our experience, the following methods are recommended for particular problem categories:
• Complex — SCRUM method, specifically designed to deal with a high level of volatility and uncertainty

• Complicated — e.g., Kanban and SCRUM methods, as the category covers sophisticated problems, requiring careful analysis, highly expert knowledge to solve, and some amount of probing different solutions, as there is no one best solution
• Obvious (simple) — all of the waterfall approaches, as the category covers known problems and has best practices prepared, enabling use of a carefully preplanned approach
• Chaotic — no method recommended, due to complete unpredictability of the systems’ behavior

Problems in the area of Enterprise Architecture tend to fulfill the criteria for simple and complicated categories, especially when architecture is already present in the organization, as it aims at increasing the level of order and predictability. The cause-and-effect relationships are present and possible to discern, and the only case in which the problems might become complex or chaotic is high volatility of the environment (usually combined with lack of knowledge about the organization at hand and its exterior). To which domain a particular problem belongs depends, inter alia, on the expertise in the organization, its architecture maturity, scope of the project, and additional constraints imposed. The task to classify the problem is up to the Project Manager.
4. Choosing an Enterprise Architecture Framework

In the area of Enterprise Architecture, the choice to be made is between one of different architecture frameworks. There are at least a few different major frameworks which provide tools and resources for Enterprise Architects (including the Zachman Framework for Enterprise Architecture™ and the Federal Enterprise Architecture (FEA)). However, not all of them are useful in the case of Architecture Project Management. This is the consequence of the different focus of each of the frameworks. As Architecture Project Management is, in fact, a process of creating an architecture, only the frameworks which provide methods of creating architectures should be taken into consideration. This is where the TOGAF Framework, as compared to other frameworks, excels, thanks to its detailed description of the ADM.
Example 3-7

In Project A, the Project Manager has no clear understanding what views are necessary to achieve the goals of the project, making it a complicated problem. He therefore has decided to include on “overview” stage at the beginning, enabling him to determine scope, which will allow completion of the project in the set timeframe and with set resources. After the thorough analysis of two applications during this phase, he confirmed with the Executive what is feasible to do in the following stages and will address the existing business need of the Executive. Later on, the Project Manager has decided to adopt an iterative approach by splitting the 50 applications used into groups of eight, which will be assessed in every two-week iteration.

In Project E, the Project Manager has to deliver precisely described artifacts and products to a set date, making the problem a simple one, assuming the presence of necessary resources. Failure to do so will result in potentially costly delays in the project, including fines for not complying with regulatory requirements, as the architecture stream is on the critical path. Therefore, the Project Manager has adopted the preplanned approach with time-bound stages with some buffer, focusing initially on the baseline (baseline first approach). This plan has been assessed as feasible by the external consulting experts involved in the project, who have participated in similar projects in the past. Nevertheless, the risk has been assessed and communicated, and its significant part has been transferred to the consulting firm in the form of additional provisions in the contract.
In this document we assume the Architecture Projects are conducted according to the TOGAF Framework, supplemented with practices stemming from the most popular Project Management methods.
