sections.title_en: 3.1.6. Design and Appoint the Project Management Team
sections.title_zh: 设计并任命项目管理团队
sections.translation_zh:
架构项目的项目经理并非在真空中运作，也不是单枪匹马交付产品。他们借助企业内其他机构提供的支持，并受这些机构约束，以确保组织目标得以实现。他们是团队的一部分，共同交付产品、为组织实现收益。

在 PRINCE2 中，他们是一个项目管理团队（Project Management Team）的成员，该团队为其提供监督与支持。这些项目管理团队构成完整的项目管理结构，包括负责治理、管理与支持的机构[5]。PMBOK 中也有项目管理团队，但与 PRINCE2 相比，其范围限于项目管理与领导活动，不包含治理机构（仅与治理机构协作）。

图3-2：基于PRINCE2方法的项目团队模型简图。

**1. 架构项目中的治理**

负责产品成功交付的机构，理应最关心“确保业务得到妥善开展”（这也是 TOGAF 标准中对治理最一般的定义）。实际情况正是如此：PMBOK 中的治理机构是发起人（Sponsor）；PRINCE2 中是指导委员会（Steering Committee），由执行发起人领导——执行发起人是最终决策者，用户与供应商的代表只是可选顾问；TOGAF 标准中是架构委员会（Architecture Board），即企业内架构的赞助者。

但须牢记，架构委员会提供的治理（即架构治理，Architecture Governance）与上述另外两个机构提供的治理（即项目治理，Project Governance）类型不同。架构治理是在企业范围内管理与控制企业架构及其他架构的实践与导向；而项目治理（按 PMBOK）是一种“与组织治理模型相一致、贯穿项目生命周期的监督职能……提供全面、一致的控制项目并确保其成功的方法”。因此，架构项目应同时接受两类治理：前者使其与战略架构及子架构保持一致，后者确保项目在质量、预算与时间方面交付预期结果。

这是否意味着架构项目的项目经理应受两个不同机构监督？往往如此。但这取决于项目管理与企业架构的组织安排：组织是否已设立架构治理机构（如架构委员会）？若已设立，该架构治理机构能否同时承担项目治理角色？若未设立，且该项目是组织的首次企业架构工作，指导委员会能否在项目完成后转变为架构委员会？可能性很多，具体做法应视项目与组织特征而定。

> **示例 3-8**
>
> 项目经理受命管理项目 B（改进物流流程）。该项目由公司 CIO 赞助；业务方要求 CIO 提供最新信息，以便更好地规划与分配资源，最终缩短订单到交付的时间。CIO 主持架构委员会，委员会成员还包括参与公司物流流程的一些业务单元负责人。
>
> CIO 决定无需再设立额外机构提供项目治理，因为多数关键利益相关者已经是提供架构治理的机构成员。目前不存在相互依赖关系或计划中的后续工作，所有决策都将基于其结果作出。
>
> 因此，项目经理转向架构委员会、尤其是 CIO，请其不仅提供架构治理，还作为项目发起人提供项目治理，并在可能的情况下把其余受影响的业务负责人纳入委员会。

> **示例 3-9**
>
> 项目经理受命领导项目 E，目标是在一家银行设计目标架构，其中包括新的数据仓库与管理信息系统。该架构项目是新解决方案实施这一更大项目群的一部分，架构工作只是多个工作流之一，这些工作流彼此密切相关、相互依赖。对架构项目而言尤其如此，因为它起着后续工作的使能作用。项目由整个信息系统转型举措的项目群管理层发起，该管理层与架构委员会没有任何关联。项目受预算、时间框架与范围的严格约束，要求严格遵循计划与要求。
>
> 在此情况下，项目经理向项目群管理层负责，同时必须遵守组织中架构委员会施加的规则与约束。视问题类型而定——是与架构相关，还是与项目管理及执行相关——他必须遵循不同的上报路径。

**2. 架构项目中项目经理的支持**

有时架构项目规模过大、过于复杂，单个项目经理即便有企业领导层支持也难以承担与管理；此外，某些项目可能需要项目经理本人不具备的特定技能与能力。这就需要架构委员会或其他治理机构之外的人员，他们最终成为项目管理团队的核心。

TOGAF 标准在 TOGAF® 系列指南：架构技能框架 [G198] 中描述了通常属于“架构团队”的角色：企业架构角色与技能类别，以及企业架构角色与技能定义。这些角色既包括负责治理架构与支持项目的角色，也包括负责运营管理与交付的角色（各域架构师与解决方案设计师）。这些角色属于架构能力框架，与项目管理团队的结构相互独立。TOGAF 标准未描述支持项目的项目管理团队应如何配备或组织，但项目管理方法提供了一些提示。

PMBOK 在第 2.3 节提供了关于项目团队的一般信息[6]，关于项目管理团队（项目团队中负责项目管理与领导活动的子集）的信息则几乎没有。它指出，项目团队唯一不变的是项目经理作为团队领导者的角色，这给了项目经理很大自由。在构思项目团队结构时应考虑的因素，PMBOK 提及文化、范围、地点与组织结构；除给出项目团队中某些可能角色的信息（详见 PMBOK 指南 §2.3）与支持项目经理决策及管理流程的工具（见 PMBOK 指南 §9）外，它未就如何组织团队提供指南。

PRINCE2 更为具体，指出团队经理（team managers）——由项目经理指派、负责交付产品的人，其产品在项目工作包（Project Work Package）中定义（关于项目工作包与工作包，见 2.3 节）；以及项目支持（Project Support）人员（通常属于项目管理办公室），其职责限于行政与运营支持，并就项目管理工具与技术提供指导。

是否设置团队经理、如何界定其角色与职责，完全由项目经理决定（但该决定应经提供项目治理的机构批准），不过不应草率决定，因为它影响项目中工作的划分方式。应考虑的因素包括：

- 项目的估计范围，涉及项目将影响的所有域与分段；
- 项目约束，尤其是时间框架；
- 所涉团队的规模。

基于我们对架构项目的了解以及对项目管理方法的一般知识，至少可以提出两种选择团队经理的方式：

- **按架构域**：各团队经理分别是对业务、数据、应用或技术架构负责的架构师；
- **按企业连续统一体层级**：各团队经理分别是对项目所影响的不同分段或解决方案负责的架构师（但我们建议架构项目的范围清晰限定在战略、分段或能力层级之一）。

> **示例 3-10**
>
> 在项目 E 中，架构只是大型项目的一个工作流。架构工作流可以使用通用的项目支持团队（PMO）处理会议安排或管理工作流存储库等行政事务。因此，架构工作流负责人认为不需要单独的支持人员。

团队结构在项目启动阶段确立。但在项目初期阶段之后，应对项目团队结构进行评审，并可按变化的需要进行调整。

**3. 架构项目中的交付团队**

最后一组人员（但重要性不亚于前述各组）是从事运营性执行、承担项目交付物工作的人。他们按团队组织，由项目经理直接管理或由团队级经理管理，视具体项目的项目管理结构而定。

参与项目的人员选择对项目成功至关重要，主要取决于架构项目的目标与范围以及可用资源。TOGAF® 系列指南：架构技能框架 [G198] 有助于规划与选择交付团队成员；该领域更通用的技术见 PMBOK 指南 [PMBOK, §9]。

> **示例 3-11**
>
> 在项目 B 中，交付团队从可用资源中挑选。目标是确保团队技能足够强，能以一次工作坊覆盖每个业务子单元。这需要周密规划，并在团队内形成技能与关于当前信息流及系统的知识的恰当组合。
>
> 交付团队由以下人员组成：
>
> - **企业架构师**——同时担任项目经理；负责项目规划、吸引利益相关者参与、准备模板、评审工作产品与准备最终交付物；还会积极参与业务工作坊，以确保其适用（fit-for-purpose）
> - **业务流程分析师**——负责主持业务工作坊，并按与企业架构师共同制定的方法记录工作坊结果
> - **物流信息系统架构师**——积极参与业务工作坊，提供关于当前 IT 系统能力及其发展潜力的知识

source_units.text_en: 3.1.6. Design and Appoint the Project Management Team

Project Managers of Architecture Projects do not operate in a void and do not deliver products singlehandedly. They use support provided by other institutions within an enterprise and are regulated by them in order to ensure that the goals of the organization are met. They are part of the team, working together to deliver the products and realize the benefits for the organization.

In PRINCE2, they are part of a Project Management Team, which provides them with oversight and support. These Project Management Teams are the whole Project Management structure comprising bodies responsible for governance,[5] management, and support. There are also Project Management Teams in PMBOK, but, in comparison to PRINCE2, they are limited to Project Management and leadership activities, and do not include governance bodies (they only cooperate with them).
Figure 3-2: Simplified Chart Representing Model Project Team Based on the PRINCE2 Method
1. Governance in Architecture Projects

The bodies which are responsible for successful delivery of the product should naturally be the ones most interested in “ensuring that the business is conducted properly” (which is the most general definition of governance, found also in the TOGAF Standard). This is exactly the case: the governing body in the case of PMBOK is the Sponsor, in PRINCE2 it is the Steering Committee, led by an Executive (who is the ultimate decision-maker, only advised by optional representatives of users and suppliers), and in the TOGAF Standard it is the Architecture Board (which is a sponsor of architecture in an enterprise).

It is necessary to bear in mind, though, that there is a difference in the type of governance provided by the Architecture Board (i.e., Architecture Governance) and the other two bodies mentioned (i.e., Project Governance). Architecture Governance is the practice and orientation by which Enterprise Architectures and other architectures are managed and controlled at an enterprise-wide level, while Project Governance (according to PMBOK) is an “oversight function that is aligned with the organization’s governance model and that encompasses the project lifecycle … providing a comprehensive, consistent method of controlling the project and ensuring its success”. As a result, Architecture Projects should be subject to both types of governance, first allowing to provide alignment with strategic architecture and sub-architectures, second to ensure that the project delivers expected results in terms of quality, budget, and time.

Does this mean that the Project Manager on the Architecture Project should be overseen by two different bodies? Often yes. However, it depends on the Project Management and Enterprise Architecture organization. Is the architecture governance body (such as the Architecture Board) already established in the organization? If it is, can the architecture governance body take the role of project governance as well? If it is not and the project is the organization’s initial Enterprise Architecture effort, can the Steering Committee transform into an Architecture Board after the project is completed? There are many possibilities and the approach should be different depending on project and organization characteristics.
Example 3-8

The Project Manager has been tasked with managing Project B (improve logistics process). The project is sponsored by the CIO of the company, who has been tasked by the business to provide current information to allow for better planning and resource allocation, to shorten order-to- delivery time as an end result. The CIO presides over the Architecture Board, which also includes some leaders of business units involved in the company’s logistics process.

The CIO decided there is no need to set up additional bodies to provide project governance, as most of the key stakeholders are already part of the body providing architecture governance. There are no inter-dependencies or planned follow-ups at the moment, and all decisions will be made on the basis of its outcome.

As a result, the Project Manager turns to the Architecture Board and CIO in particular to provide not only architecture governance, but also project governance as a Sponsor of the project, and, if possible, to include the rest of the affected business leaders on the Board.
Example 3-9

The Project Manager has been ordered to lead Project E, aiming to design the to-be architecture in a bank, which includes new data warehouse and management information systems. The Architecture Project is part of a larger program of new solution implementation, making architecture effort only one of multiple streams, which are closely related and dependent on each other. This is especially true for the Architecture Project, which functions as an enabler for

further work. The project has been initiated by the Program Management of the whole information system transformation initiative, which is not in any way connected with the Architecture Board. It is strictly bound by budget, timeframe, and scope, requiring strict adherence to the plans and requirements.

The Project Manager is responsible in this case to the Program Management, while simultaneously has to adhere to the rules and constraints imposed by the Architecture Board in the organization. Depending on the type of issue, whether it is connected with architecture, or Project Management and execution, he is obliged to follow different escalation routes.
2. Project Manager’s Support in Architecture Projects

Sometimes, Architecture Projects are too big and complex for a single Project Manager to undertake and manage, even with support provided from the enterprise leadership. Furthermore, some projects may require specific skills and competencies, which are not possessed by the Project Manager designated to lead the project. This creates the need for additional people, other than those in the Architecture Board or other governing body, who ultimately become the core of the Project Management Team.

The TOGAF Standard describes the roles that are usually part of an “architecture team” in the TOGAF Series Guide: Architecture Skills Framework [G198]: Enterprise Architecture Role and Skill Categories, and Enterprise Architecture Role and Skill Definitions. These include both roles responsible for governing the architecture and supporting the project and roles responsible for operational management and delivery (architects for different domains and solution designers). These roles are part of the Architecture Capability Framework and are separate from the structure of a Project Management Team. The TOGAF Standard does not describe how the Project Management Team supporting the project should be staffed or organized. However, some hints are provided in the Project Management methods.

PMBOK provides general information about Project Teams[6] in Section 2.3 and hardly any regarding Project Management Team (a subset of Project Team responsible for the Project Management and leadership activities). It says that the only constant with regards to the Project Team is Project Manager’s role as its leader, giving a lot of freedom to the Project Manager. Among the factors which should be considered while devising the Project Team structure, PMBOK mentions culture, scope, location, and organizational structure. It does not provide guidelines on how it should be organized, other than giving information on some of possible roles within the Project Team (for more information, see §2.3 of the PMBOK Guide) and tools supporting the Project Manager’s decision-making and management processes (see §9 of the PMBOK Guide).

PRINCE2 is more specific and points out team managers, who are people responsible for delivery of products assigned by the Project Manager, as defined in the Project Work Packages later on (for more information on Project Work Packages and Work Packages, see Section 2.3) and people being part of Project Support (usually as part of the Project Management Office), whose duties are limited to support in administration and operations and providing guidance regarding Project Management tools and techniques).

The decision on whether to appoint team managers, how to define their roles and duties, is entirely up to the Project Manager (but this decision should be approved by the bodies providing project governance), but shouldn’t be made without serious consideration, as it impacts how the work will be divided during the project. The factors, which should be considered are, among others:
• Estimated scope of the project, with regard to both domains and segments, that will be affected by the project
• Project constraints, especially with regard to timeframe
• Size of the team involved
Based on what we know about Architecture Projects and having a general knowledge of Project Management methods, it is possible to propose at least two ways of selecting team managers:
• By architecture domain, where particular team managers are architects responsible for either business, data, application, or technology architecture

• By enterprise continuum level, where particular team managers are architects responsible for different segments or solutions, which are affected by the project (however, we recommend that the Architecture Project has a clear scope restricted to one of the levels: strategic, segment, or capability)
Example 3-10

In Project E, architecture is just one of work streams of a large project. The architecture work stream can use a general Project Support team (PMO) for administrative tasks such as setting up meetings or managing the work stream repository. Therefore, the architecture work stream leader decided he would not need any separate support staff.
The team structure is established in the Project Start-up stage. However, after the initial stages of the project, the Project Team structure should be reviewed and may be adapted to changing needs.
3. Delivery Team in Architecture Projects

The last group (but no less important than those mentioned earlier) are people engaged in operational execution by working on project deliverables. They are organized in teams, managed by the Project Manager directly or team-level managers, depending on the Project Management structure in a particular project.

Selection of people to be involved in the project is critical to its success. It depends mainly on the goals and scope of the Architecture Project, and the resources available. The TOGAF® Series Guide: Architecture Skills Framework [G198] can be helpful in planning and selecting delivery team members. More general techniques in this area are described in the PMBOK Guide [PMBOK, §9].
Example 3-11

In Project B, the delivery team was selected among available resources. The aim was to ensure the team has skills strong enough to cover each of the business subunits with a single workshop. This required careful planning and the right mix of skills and knowledge of current information flows and systems within the team.
The delivery team consisted of:

• Enterprise Architect — who was also the Project Manager; responsible for planning the project, engaging stakeholders, preparing templates, reviewing work products, and preparing final deliverables; would also take an active part in business workshops to ensure they are fit-for-purpose
• Business Process Analyst — who would facilitate business workshops and document their results in line with the approach developed with the Enterprise Architect
• Logistics Information Systems Architect — who would take an active part in business workshops and provide knowledge on the current IT systems capabilities and their development potential

sections.translation_zh:
按 PRINCE2 与 PMBOK，当汇总项目假设的文档编制完成并获得批准时，项目即获得授权。该文档至少应界定项目的高层边界。

按 PRINCE2，项目任务书（Project Brief）是描述项目目的、成本、时间与绩效要求以及约束的陈述。

按 PMBOK，项目章程（Project Charter）获批时项目即获授权。项目章程记录业务需要、假设、约束、对客户需要的理解与高层要求，以及拟由项目满足的新产品、服务或结果。

该文档由执行发起人发布，正式授权项目存在，并授予项目经理动用组织资源开展项目活动的权力。建议项目经理参与项目章程的编制，以获得对项目要求的基础性理解；这种理解有助于更有效地把资源分配到项目活动。

文档中的信息对项目经理规划关键里程碑、详细进度以及规划阶段执行特定任务所需的关键资源具有价值；在项目结束时，这些信息对核实项目是否在规定的时间、成本、质量与范围容差内交付预期结果也很重要。文档所含信息可随规划阶段工作的进展而更新。

架构项目开始时所需信息的类型与范围，以及这些信息将纳入哪些文档，取决于开展项目的组织所采用的项目管理规则与原则。

> **示例 3-12**
>
> 在项目 D 中，项目经理利用项目任务书中的信息编制了启动演示，并召开会议，向架构项目的关键利益相关者说明项目范围、要解决的业务需要以及所受约束。此外，项目经理还利用这些信息规划关键里程碑，并编制架构项目的详细进度。

source_units.text_en: 3.1.7. Assemble the Project Brief

According to PRINCE2 and PMBOK, the project becomes authorized when a document summarizing the project’s assumptions is assembled and approved. At minimum, the document should define the high-level boundaries of the project.
According to PRINCE2, the Project Brief is a statement that describes the purpose, cost, time, and performance requirements, and constraints for a project.

According to PMBOK, the project becomes authorized when the Project Charter is approved. The Project Charter documents the business needs, assumptions, constraints, the understanding of the customer’s needs and high-level requirements, and the new product, service, or result that it is intended to satisfy.

The document is issued by the Executive that formally authorizes the existence of a project and provides the Project Manager with the authority to apply organizational resources to project activities. It is recommended that the Project Manager participates in the development of the Project Charter to obtain a foundational understanding of the project requirements. This understanding will better allow for efficient resources allocation to project activities.

The information from the document is relevant for the Project Manager to plan key milestones, a detailed schedule, as well as key resources essential to perform particular tasks in the planning phase. They are also important at the end of the project in order to verify whether the project delivered the desired results within the specified tolerances of time, cost, quality, and scope. The information included in the document may be updated along with the progress of work in the planning phase.

The type and scope of the information needed at the beginning of an Architecture Project, as well as documents that they will be included in, depends on the Project Management rules and principles adopted in the organization conducting the project.
Example 3-12

In Project D, the Project Manager utilized the information presented in the Project Brief to develop a kick-off presentation and conduct a meeting informing key stakeholders of the Architecture Project about its scope, business needs to be addressed, as well as imposed constraints. Furthermore, the information was utilized by the Project Manager to plan key milestones and develop a detailed schedule for the Architecture Project.

sections.translation_zh:
在完成初步的项目启动——选择项目方法并任命项目管理团队——之后，项目经理确定项目将如何被管理。在 PRINCE2 中，这称为编制管理策略（Management Strategy）；在 PMBOK 中，它是制定项目章程流程的一部分。“定义管理方法”步骤包括确定以下方面的做法：

- 风险管理
- 质量管理
- 利益相关者与沟通管理
- 项目控制

**1. 风险管理方法**

作为项目启动的一部分，项目经理确定风险管理方法，并与项目治理机构确认。风险管理方法通常包括以下步骤：

- 风险识别与分类；
- 风险分析（定性及定量）；
- 风险缓解与应对策略设计；
- 风险监控。

项目经理还在项目开始时进行初始风险评估，包括风险识别、分类、分析与应对设计。该活动的关键成果是风险日志（risk log），记录已识别风险及其特征以及设计的应对措施。风险日志将在整个项目中用于监控与管理风险；详见 3.4 节。关于项目风险管理技术的更多信息，参见 PMBOK 指南 §11。

> **示例 3-13**
>
> 在项目 E 中，初始风险评估先在工作流层面进行，然后在项目层面进行（项目由若干工作流组成）。在架构工作流中，初始风险评估先在交付物层面进行，然后汇总并在工作流层面扩展。
>
> 风险日志示例参见 3.4.5 节的示例。

> 从项目管理角度看，风险管理关注的是影响项目目标实现的风险。请注意，架构项目还必须处理另一类关键风险——与架构愿景及其实现相关的企业风险。这类风险可称为“架构风险”（architecture risk），必须加以管理与缓解。管理架构风险的技术与项目风险类似，见 TOGAF 标准——ADM 技术：风险管理。

**2. 质量管理方法**

作为项目启动的一部分，项目经理确定质量管理方法，并与项目治理机构确认。质量管理方法应与组织的质量管理体系相容。它通常应确立：

- 项目交付物的关键质量特性——交付物移交时用于评估符合性的条件；
- 文档要求——这些质量特性如何被记录，以便进行符合性检查；
- 质量保证流程——这些质量特性如何被检查是否符合（交付物移交前与移交时）。

质量管理方法将在整个项目中应用。所确立的准则对阶段收尾与项目收尾活动至关重要（见 3.5 节与 3.6 节）。关于项目质量管理技术的更多信息，参见 PMBOK 指南 §8。

> **示例 3-14**
>
> 在项目 E 中，每项项目交付物都用一份交付物章程（Deliverable Charter）来描述。交付物章程界定交付物名称、范围、所需输入、验收标准与验收流程。设计了两类验收流程——一类用于文档交付物（分析、架构等），一类用于软件交付物，后者包含系统测试方法。
>
> 文档验收流程包括五个步骤：交付物初次移交、初次交付物评审（两周）、评审会议（一天）、交付物修订（两周）、最终交付物评审（一周）。假定最终交付物评审确认交付物符合质量要求。
>
> 验收流程与交付物章程由项目治理机构讨论并接受。

**3. 利益相关者与沟通管理方法**

TOGAF ADM 阶段 A 包括利益相关者识别以及确定利益相关者沟通方法。这是项目经理在架构项目启动期间必须确保的核心活动之一。

具体而言，项目经理应：

- 识别所有利益相关者及其对最终企业架构的关注点；
- 确定利益相关者沟通管理方法；
- 确定利益相关者参与交付物；
- 把上述信息记录为利益相关者图（stakeholder map）与沟通计划。

TOGAF 的利益相关者管理技术能满足妥善管理利益相关者方法的需要，该技术见 TOGAF 标准——ADM 技术：利益相关者管理。PMBOK 采用类似方法，见项目利益相关者管理（§13）。

输出交付物——利益相关者图与沟通计划——由项目经理在项目执行与控制期间使用。利益相关者图也是参与项目的企业架构师了解参与交付物（目录、矩阵、图）的重要知识来源。

> **示例 3-15**
>
> 在项目 A 中，在项目启动与 ADM 阶段 A 期间，项目经理采用 TOGAF 标准所述方法来管理利益相关者。他首先识别利益相关者，然后把关注点相同的利益相关者归入利益相关者群体（如 C 级管理层、IT 运营），再使用权力—利益矩阵定义利益相关者沟通方法。他为四个群体分别定义了项目团队与每个群体沟通的方式与频率（例如，利益水平低且权力低的利益相关者只通过电子邮件收到每周项目简报）。
>
> 最后，项目经理定义了利益相关者参与交付物，并创建了利益相关者图矩阵，将其加入项目沟通计划。

**4. 项目控制方法**

项目控制界定为确保项目妥善执行与项目管理有效性所需的控制程度。项目控制应在项目启动期间界定。

PRINCE2 把项目控制界定为：

- 各项目管理层级之间沟通的频率与形式；
- 阶段数量，因而也是阶段末评估的次数；
- 捕获与分析问题及变更的机制；
- 上报例外（exception）的机制；
- 授权委托的容差；
- 如何监控从一管理层级向另一管理层级的授权委托。

项目控制应作为管理方法的一部分加以界定，并在整个项目中执行（见 3.4 节）。

> **示例 3-16**
>
> 在项目 A 启动期间，项目经理定义了几项项目控制：
>
> - 为架构项目团队设立每周状态报告会议。
> - 决定把被分析的应用划分为三个包（原文为“tree packages”，按“three”理解），并为每个包指派负责的应用架构师。
> - 规定所有问题都登记在共享问题日志中，所有变更都登记在共享变更日志中，形式为项目内网存储库中的 Excel 电子表格。

source_units.text_en: 3.1.8. Define the Management Approach

After initial project start-up — selecting the project approach and appointing the Project Management Team — the Project Manager determines how the project will be managed. In PRINCE2, it is called preparing a Management Strategy. In PMBOK, it is a part of the Develop Project Charter process. The Define the Management Approach step includes determining an approach to:
• Risk management
• Quality management
• Stakeholder and communication management
• Project controls
1. Risk Management Approach

As part of project initiation, the Project Manager determines the risk management approach and confirms it with the project governance body. Typically, an approach to risk management includes the following steps:
• Risk identification and classification
• Risk analysis (qualitative and quantitative)
• Risk mitigation and response strategy design
• Risk monitoring

The Project Manager also performs an initial risk assessment, which includes risk identification, classification, analysis, and design at the beginning of the project. The key result of this activity is a risk log, which documents identified risks and their characteristics together with designed responses. The risk log will be used throughout the project to monitor and manage risk; see Section 3.4 for details.
For more information on project risk management techniques, refer to the PMBOK Guide, §11.
Example 3-13

In Project E, initial risk assessment is performed first on a work stream level, then on the project level (the project consists of a few work streams). In the architecture work stream, initial risk assessment is performed on a deliverable level, then consolidated and extended on the work stream level.
For a risk log example, refer to the example in Section 3.4.5.

Risk management from the Project Management perspective is concerned with risks to meeting projects goals. Please note that the Architecture Project has to deal with another key type of risk — risk to the enterprise associated with the Architecture Vision and related to implementing it. This type of risk — we can call it “architecture risk” — has to be managed and mitigated. Techniques of managing architecture risk are similar to that applied to project risk; they are described in the TOGAF Standard — ADM Techniques: Risk Management.
2. Quality Management Approach

As part of project initiation, the Project Manager determines the quality management approach and confirms it with the project governance body. The quality management approach should be compatible with the organization’s quality management system. Typically, it should establish:
• Key quality characteristics of the project deliverables — conditions that would be used to assess conformance when the deliverable is handed over
• Documentation requirements — how these quality characteristics would be documented to allow for conformance checks
• Quality assurance processes — how these quality characteristics would be checked for conformance (before and on deliverable handover)
The quality management approach will be used throughout the project. Established criteria are key for stage and project closing activities (see Section 3.5, and Section 3.6).
For more information on project quality management techniques, refer to the PMBOK Guide, §8.
Example 3-14

In Project E, each of the project deliverables is described with a Deliverable Charter. The Deliverable Charter defines the deliverable name, its scope, required inputs, acceptance criteria, and acceptance process. Two types of acceptance processes are designed — one for documentation deliverables (analysis, architecture, etc.) and one for software deliverables which includes the system testing approach.
The document acceptance process consists of five steps: initial hand over of the deliverable, initial deliverable review (two weeks), review meeting (one day), deliverable revision (two
weeks), final deliverable review (one week). It is assumed that the final deliverable review confirms the deliverable’s conformance to quality requirements.
Acceptance processes and Deliverable Charters are discussed and accepted by the project governing body.
3. Stakeholder and Communication Management Approach

TOGAF ADM Phase A includes stakeholder identification and determining an approach to stakeholder communication. It is one of the core activities that the Project Manager has to assure during the Architecture Project initiation.
Specifically, the Project Manager should:
• Identify all stakeholders and their concerns about the resulting Enterprise Architecture
• Determine the stakeholder communication management approach
• Determine the stakeholder engagement deliverables
• Document all the above information in a form of stakeholder map and communication plan

The TOGAF stakeholder management technique fulfills needs related to the proper stakeholder management approach. This technique is described in the TOGAF Standard — ADM Techniques: Stakeholder Management. PMBOK uses a similar approach, which is described in Project Stakeholder Management (§13).
Example 3-15

In Project A, during initiation of the project and Phase A of the ADM, the Project Manager uses the approach described in the TOGAF Standard to manage stakeholders. At first he identified the stakeholders, then he grouped the stakeholders with common concerns into stakeholder groups (e.g., C-level management, IT operations), then he defined the stakeholder communication approach using the power-interest matrix. He defined for each of four groups how and how often the Project Team would communicate with each of the four groups. (e.g., the stakeholders with low level of interest and low power receive only the weekly project brief on their emails). At the end, the Project Manager defined the stakeholder engagement deliverables and created the stakeholder map matrix. He added this matrix to the project communication plan.

The output deliverables stakeholder maps and communication plans are used by the Project Manager during project execution and control. The stakeholder map is also the important source of knowledge about engagement deliverables (catalogs, matrices diagrams) for Enterprise Architects that participate in the project.
4. Project Controls Approach

Project controls define the level of control that is demanded to ensure proper project execution and the effectiveness of Project Management. Project controls should be defined during initiation of the project.
PRINCE2 defines project controls as:
• The frequency and format of communication between the Project Management levels
• The number of stages and hence end stage assessments
• Mechanisms to capture and analyze issues and changes
• Mechanisms to escalate exceptions
• Tolerances for delegated authority
• How delegated authority from one level of management to another will be monitored
Project controls should be defined as part of the management approach. They are executed throughout the project (see Section 3.4).
Example 3-16
During the initiation of Project A, the Project Manager defined several project controls:
• He set up weekly status report meetings for the Architecture Project Team.
• He decided to divide the analyzed applications to tree packages and assign the responsible application architect for each package.
• He stated that all issues will be registered in a shared issue log and all changes will be registered in a shared change log in the form of Excel® spreadsheets in the project intranet repository.

sections.translation_zh:
项目规划是把项目范围界定并拆分为可管理任务，并为这些任务确定进度与质量标准。可以说，这是项目经理在项目开始时最重要的工作。按 PRINCE2，要有计划才能控制任何事情——就架构项目而言我们同意这一观点。

TOGAF ADM 阶段 A 以编制并批准架构工作说明书（Statement of Architecture Work）结束，其中包含“项目计划与进度”。TOGAF 标准未深入细节，也未描述规划技术。本文档建议按以下活动顺序编制进度，并将其纳入架构工作说明书。

我们建议按以下活动顺序编制架构项目进度与架构工作说明书：

- 定义架构项目范围；
- 定义架构项目的最终产品及其验收标准；
- 定义项目交付物；
- 定义项目排除项、约束与假设；
- 细化架构项目范围；
- 创建工作分解结构（WBS）；
- 编制架构项目计划与进度（排列活动顺序、估算活动资源与工期、制定进度）；
- 汇总架构工作说明书并获得批准。

这些活动将在以下各小节描述。

在 TOGAF 标准中，阶段 A 全程会交付不少重要的（非管理类）工作产品。这些工作产品可能对架构项目范围产生重大影响，应在编制工作分解结构与项目计划之前完成，包括：

- **评估能力与评估业务转型就绪度**——项目规划应基于对变革复杂度与变革就绪度的这一初步评估；
- **确认并细化架构原则（包括业务原则）**——项目规划应考虑架构原则；
- **制定架构愿景**——项目规划应基于架构愿景所勾勒的基线与目标架构；
- **定义目标架构价值主张与 KPI，并识别业务转型风险与缓解活动**——这些虽与项目范围无直接关系，但部分价值主张与业务转型风险缓解活动可能影响项目范围，应在项目规划中予以考虑。

上述工作产品可能对架构项目范围产生重大影响，应在编制工作分解结构与项目计划之前完成。这些工作产品范围宽泛，但通常只需在高层次产出，以便刚好提供规划后续工作、进入更详细层级所需的信息。

source_units.text_en: 3.2. Architecture Project Planning

Project planning is about defining and splitting the project’s scope into manageable tasks with a defined schedule and quality criteria. Arguably, it is the most important task of the Project Manager at the project start. According to PRINCE2, a plan is necessary to control anything – and we agree with regard to Architecture Projects.

TOGAF ADM Phase A ends with development and approval of the Statement of Architecture Work, which includes a “project plan and schedule”. It does not go into detail and omits a planning techniques description. In this document, we recommend a sequence of activities that allows creation of a schedule and includes it in the Statement of Architecture Work.
We recommend the following sequence of activities to develop the Architecture Project schedule and
Statement of Architecture Work:
• Define the Architecture Project Scope
• Define the Final Product of the Architecture Project and its Acceptance Criteria
• Define the Project Deliverables
• Define the Project Exclusions, Constraints, and Assumptions
• Detail the Architecture Project Scope
• Create the Work Breakdown Structure
• Develop the Architecture Project Plan and Schedule (sequence activities, estimate activity resources and durations, develop schedule)
• Consolidate the Statement of Architecture Work and Secure Approval
These activities are described in the following subsections.

In the TOGAF Standard, there are quite a few essential (non-management) work products delivered throughout Phase A. These work products can have a great impact on the Architecture Project Scope and should be completed before working on the Work Breakdown Structure and Project Plan. They include:
• Evaluate Capabilities and Assess Readiness for Business Transformation – project planning should be based on this preliminary assessment of change complexity and readiness for change
• Confirm and Elaborate Architecture Principles, including Business Principles – project planning should take into account Architecture Principles
• Develop Architecture Vision – project planning should be based on baseline and target architectures outlined in the Architecture Vision

• Define the Target Architecture Value Propositions and KPIs and Identify the Business Transformation Risks and Mitigation Activities – while not directly related to Project Scope, some of the value propositions and business transformation risk mitigation activities may impact the Project Scope and should be taken into account in project planning

The above work products can have a great impact on the Architecture Project Scope and should be completed before working on the Work Breakdown Structure and Project Plan. These work products are wide in scope, but they are usually produced at a very high level, to allow just enough information to plan further work and get to a more detailed level.

sections.translation_zh:
定义架构项目及其范围是最重要的活动，应极为谨慎并保持清醒地开展。该活动的输出将对项目目标的理解与实现产生重大影响。

> 请注意，架构项目范围的定义比 TOGAF ADM 阶段 A 中“定义范围”步骤所述更宽。“定义范围”ADM 步骤描述的是基线架构与目标架构工作范围内外的内容；而架构项目范围按项目管理方法的含义，指为实现项目目标而要执行的工作范围。当然，执行“定义范围”ADM 步骤是理解和界定架构项目范围的关键初始任务。

架构项目的范围应运用 ADM 的范围定义活动以及阶段 A 的其他重要输出（如架构愿景）来界定（见 3.2 节开头的清单）。按 TOGAF 标准，关键在于界定将覆盖的架构全景层级、广度与时间范围（如原文图 2-1 所示）；另见 TOGAF 标准——架构开发方法阶段 A：架构愿景（定义范围）以及 TOGAF 标准——应用 ADM：跨越架构全景应用 ADM。

项目管理方法提供的工具与技术同样可用于界定详细的项目范围与项目计划；其中最重要的在以下各小节介绍。

作为范围定义的一部分，应编制一份架构项目概述（Architecture Project Description），即对项目下将开展的工作及项目目标的简要概括。上述 ADM 任务的全部输出应汇总并一并分析，以编制项目范围说明书（Project Scope Statement）——对范围、主要交付物、假设与约束的描述。

> **示例 3-17**
>
> 在项目 A 中，完成 ADM 阶段 A 的关键任务后，项目经理已具备足够知识来编制架构项目描述。他决定先定义项目的主要目标，得出：“评估现有应用组合并提出改进选项。”
>
> 在定义主要目标之后，他编制了更详细的架构项目描述：
>
> 描述应用全景并识别 IT 改进选项。约有 50 个不同规模的应用（精确数量在项目执行期间确定），多为定制开发。关键关注点：
>
> - 确定应用之间的关系与数据流
> - 映射应用能力（重叠与缺口）
> - 识别应用开发的关键技术约束
>
> 所需视图待定。改进选项应包含带优先级的举措。

source_units.text_en: 3.2.1. Define the Architecture Project Scope

Defining the Architecture Project and its scope is the most important activity which should be performed with great care and awareness. The output of this activity will have significant impact on the understanding and achievement of the project’s goals.

Note that the definition of an Architecture Project Scope is broader than described in the Define Scope step of the TOGAF ADM Phase A. The Define Scope ADM step describes what is in the scope of the Baseline Architecture and Target Architecture efforts. The Architecture Project Scope, in line with the Project Management methods, means the scope of work which is to be performed in order to achieve the project’s goals. Of course, performing the Define Scope ADM step is a critical initial task to understand and define the Architecture Project Scope.

The scope of the Architecture Project should be defined using the ADM scope definition activities and other essential Phase A outputs, such as the Architecture Vision (see the list in Section 3.2). According to the TOGAF Standard, it is critical to define what level of the Architecture Landscape, breadth and time will be covered (as shown Figure 2-1); also see TOGAF Standard — Architecture Development Method Phase A: Architecture Vision (Define Scope) and the TOGAF Standard — Applying the ADM: Applying the ADM Across the Architecture Landscape.]

The Project Management methods provide tools and techniques which too can be used during definition of the detailed Project Scope and Project Plan; the most important of them are presented in the following subsections.

As part of the scope definition, a summary Architecture Project Description should be created. The Architecture Project Description is a short summary of the work that will be performed under the project along with the project’s goals. All outputs from the above ADM tasks should be gathered and analyzed together in order to prepare the Project Scope Statement that is the description of the scope, major deliverables, assumptions, and constraints.
Example 3-17

In Project A, after completion of the essential tasks from the ADM Phase A, the Project Manager had enough knowledge to prepare a description of the Architecture Project. He decided to start by defining the main goal of the project and came up with the following: Assess current application portfolio and recommend improvement options.
After that, he defined the main goal, he prepared a more detailed description of the Architecture Project:

Describe the application landscape and identify IT improvement options. There are about 50 applications of different scales (precise number to be determined during project execution), mostly custom-built. Key concerns are:
• Determining relationships and data flows between applications
• Mapping application capabilities (overlaps and gaps)
• Identification of key technological constraints for application development
Required views are to be determined. Improvement options should include initiatives with assigned priorities.

sections.title_zh: 定义架构项目的最终产品及其验收标准
sections.translation_zh:
架构项目的最终产品是项目实现期间全部工作产生的主要输出。视项目目标不同，它可能是一份文档或一组相关文档，描述企业架构的现状、分析结果、建议、目标架构与路线图等。

> **示例 3-18**
>
> 在项目 A 中，项目经理确定他所管理的架构项目的最终产品是：总结当前应用组合分析及关键观察与改进建议的报告。

验收标准是架构项目最终产品被接受之前必须满足的一组条件。务必让所有项目利益相关者参与验收标准的定义，以避免项目结束时出现意外或被不当管理的期望。

> **示例 3-19**
>
> 在项目 A 中，项目经理在审阅全部文档、并与项目发起人及其他利益相关者协商后，编制了最终产品为获得验收应满足的条件清单。他决定既纳入最终产品内容的基本标准，也纳入报告本身的技术细节。
>
> 最终产品的主要验收标准如下：
>
> - 报告应以波兰语撰写，并按公司模板编制
> - 将要分析的应用的精确数量在项目执行期间确定（最初为 50 个），但不得少于 45 个
> - 应用之间的关系与数据流应采用通用记法表示，例如使用 ArchiMate 建模语言
> - 改进建议应包含路线图，列出全部举措及其优先级、估算成本与时间框架

source_units.text_en: 3.2.2. Define the Final Product of the Architecture Project and its Acceptance Criteria

The final product of the Architecture Project is the main output resulting from all work that will be performed during the project realization. Depending on the project goal it may be a document or a set of related documents that describes the current situation of, for example, the corporate architecture, results of analysis, recommendations, description of target architecture and roadmap, etc.
Example 3-18

In Project A, the Project Manager decided that the final product of the Architecture Project he is managing is: Report summarizing current application portfolio analysis along with key observations and improvement recommendations.

The acceptance criteria are a set of conditions that must to be met before the final product of the Architecture Project will be accepted. It is important to involve all projects stakeholders in the definition of project acceptance criteria in order to avoid any unexpected, mismanaged expectations at the end of the project.
Example 3-19

In Project A, after reviewing all documentation, and after consultation with the Project Sponsor and other stakeholders, the Project Manager prepared a list of conditions that the final product should meet in order to gain acceptance. He decided to include both essential criteria of the final product content as well as technical details of the report itself.
The main final product acceptance criteria are as follows:
• The report should be written in Polish and should be prepared in accordance with company templates
• The precise number of applications that are going to be analyzed is to be determined during project execution (initially it is 50), but it may not be less than 45
• Relationships and data flows between applications should be prepared in common notation; e.g., using the ArchiMate® modeling language
Recommendations for improvement should include a roadmap with all initiatives along with assigned priorities, estimated cost, and timeframe.

semantic_rules.statement_zh: 最终产品验收条件应由全部项目利益相关者参与定义。
semantic_rules.boundary_zh: 示例的波兰语、45个应用与公司模板只属于项目A，不是通用要求。

sections.translation_zh:
交付物是为完成项目或项目特定阶段而需要准备的、独特且可验证的产品、结果 [PMBOK] 与输出。交付物可以是最终产品、辅助产品或项目管理产品的一部分。定义交付物清单的目的，是更好地规划工作，并在各交付物完成后立即获得验收，而不是等到项目结束。这种方式（验收较小交付物）是降低项目结束时未达期望之风险的最佳途径。在此活动中，还应确定需交付哪些 TOGAF 文档，例如架构定义文档、架构需求规格说明书、实施与迁移计划、架构路线图等。

> **示例 3-20**
>
> 在项目 A 中，项目经理编制了项目执行期间将准备的交付物清单。他决定把最终产品拆分为更小的交付物，并纳入了一些需要在项目执行期间达成一致的附加交付物。此外，他还纳入了状态报告等管理类交付物。
>
> 项目基本交付物：
>
> - 经商定的、将作为分析对象的应用清单
> - 经商定的、将准备的所需视图清单
> - 应用之间的关系与数据流
> - 应用能力映射（重叠与缺口）
> - 应用开发关键技术约束的识别
> - 分析的关键观察
> - 改进建议
>
> 项目管理产品：
>
> - 报告要点
> - 阶段末报告
> - 风险日志
> - 问题日志
> - 变更日志
>
> 项目最终报告

source_units.text_en: 3.2.3. Define the Project Deliverables

Deliverables are unique and verifiable products, results [PMBOK], and outputs that are required to be prepared to complete a project or particular phase of the project. Deliverables may be part of the final product, any auxiliary products, or Project Management products. The aim of defining the list of

deliverables is to better plan the work and gain their acceptance right after they are completed rather than at the end of the project. This approach (acceptance of smaller deliverables) is the best way to reduce the risk of not meeting the expectations at the end of the project. During this activity it should be defined which of the TOGAF documents should be also delivered; e.g., Architecture Definition Document, Architecture Requirements Specification, Implementation and Migration Plan, Architecture Roadmap, etc.
Example 3-20

In Project A, the Project Manager prepared a list of deliverables that will be prepared during execution of the project. He decided to divide the final product into smaller deliverables and also included additional deliverables that are important to be agreed during the execution of the project. Moreover, he included management deliverables such as status reports.
Project essential deliverables:
• Agreed list of applications that will be subject of the analysis
• Agreed list of required views that will be prepared
• Relationships and data flows between applications
• Mapping application capabilities (overlaps and gaps)
• Identification of key technological constraints for application development
• Key observations from analysis
• Improvement recommendations
Project management products:
• Report highlights
• End stage report
• Risk log
• Issue log
• Change log
Project final report

sections.title_en: 3.2.4. Define the Project Exclusions, Constraints, and Assumptions
sections.title_zh: 定义项目排除项、约束与假设
sections.translation_zh:
**项目排除项（Project exclusion）**是说明哪些内容不在项目范围内的陈述，用于确认并使利益相关者知悉被排除在项目之外的内容。

**约束（Constraint）**是关于项目限制、会影响项目执行的陈述。

**假设（Assumption）**是关于被视为事实的情况的陈述。

> **示例 3-21**
>
> 在项目 A 中，项目经理基于此前分析的结果编制了排除项、约束与假设清单。示例如下。
>
> 排除项：
>
> - 改进建议将只包含带估算成本的举措
>
>   不会开展 RFI 流程以获取更可靠的成本数据。
>
> - 项目目标是分析当前应用组合及关键观察与改进建议
>
>   目标 IT 架构不在项目范围内。
>
> - 应用开发关键约束的识别将从技术视角进行
>
>   其他视角——如知识能力、人力资源、组织约束——不在项目范围内。
>
> 约束：
>
> - 项目主要由内部资源执行，但最多可为本项目投入五个全职当量（FTE）
> - 由于预算有限，无法把工作分包给组织外部
> - 最终工作产品应在 22 周内完成
>
> 假设：
>
> - 交付物将在完成后五个工作日内获得验收
> - 任何影响项目范围、预算或资源的变更请求，均由项目指导委员会批准
> - 管理层与具备相应知识的员工将投入足够时间，以收集适当信息并作出必要决策

source_units.text_en: 3.2.4. Define the Project Exclusions, Constraints, and Assumptions
Project exclusion is a statement saying what is out of scope for the project and it is used to acknowledge and make stakeholders aware of what is excluded from the project.
Constraint is a statement about the limitations of the project that affect its execution.
Assumption is a statement about facts that are considered to be true.
Example 3-21
In Project A, the Project Manager prepared a list of exclusions, constraints, and assumptions based on the results from previous analysis. Examples are listed below.
Exclusions:
• Recommendations for improvement will contain initiatives along with only estimated cost
There will be no RFI process in order to gain more reliable cost data.
• The goal of the project is to analyze the current application portfolio along with key observations and improvement recommendations
The Target IT Architecture is excluded from the Project Scope.
• Identification of key constraints for application development will be performed from a technological perspective
Other perspectives — e.g., knowledge capabilities, human resources, organizational constraints — are excluded from the Project Scope.
Constraints:
• The project is being performed mostly by internal resources, but the maximum five FTEs can be dedicated to this project
• Due to limited budget there is no possibility to subcontract work outside the organization
• The final work product should be completed within 22 weeks
Assumptions:
• Deliverables will be accepted within five working days after completion
• Any change requests affecting Project Scope, budget, or resources will be approved by the Steering Committee of the project
• Management and employees, with the appropriate knowledge, will devote sufficient time in order to collect the appropriate information and make the necessary decisions

semantic_rules.statement_zh: 假设是规划时暂按真实处理的陈述，排除项与执行限制分别记录。

sections.translation_zh:
这是把项目交付物与项目工作细分为更小、更易管理组成部分的过程 [PMBOK]。

在创建工作分解结构之前，应确定要开发哪些架构域、达到何种详细程度、构建哪些架构视图；该任务的结果应作为工作分解结构的输入。

在此任务中，还应执行以下 TOGAF ADM 活动：

- 对照业务绩效要求集合评估需产出的工作产品，确保绩效度量内建于工作产品，且与特定绩效相关的工作产品可用；
- 识别需要变更的新工作产品；
- 就哪些现有工作产品需要变更提供指导。

创建 WBS 有两种常用工具：

- **分解（Decomposition）**：用于把项目范围与项目交付物划分、细分为更小、更易管理部分的技术 [PMBOK]；
- **专家判断（Expert Judgment）**：常用于分析将项目交付物分解为更小组成部分所需的信息，以创建有效的 WBS [PMBOK]。

WBS 常以图解形式呈现，直观展示工作产品的分解。

> **示例 3-22**
>
> 在项目 A 中，项目经理使用分解技术编制了项目的 WBS。由于他此前已编制详细的项目交付物清单，他决定将其作为输入。项目经理编制的 WBS 图如下。

source_units.text_en: 3.2.6. Create the Work Breakdown Structure
This is the process of subdividing project deliverables and project work into smaller, more manageable components [PMBOK].

It should be determined which architecture domains should be developed, to what level of detail, and which architecture views should be built prior to creating the Work Breakdown Structure, and the result of this task should be an input to the Work Breakdown Structure.
During this task, the following TOGAF ADM activities should be also performed:

• Assess work products that are required to be produced against the set of business performance requirements, ensuring performance metrics are built into the work products, and specific performance-related work products are available
• Identify new work products that will need to be changed
• Provide direction on which existing work products will need to be changed
There are two common tools used to create the Work Breakdown Structure:
• Decomposition is a technique used for dividing and subdividing the Project Scope and project deliverables into smaller, more manageable parts [PMBOK]

• Expert Judgment is often used to analyze the information needed to decompose the project deliverables down into smaller component parts in order to create an effective Work Breakdown Structure [PMBOK]
The Work Breakdown Structure is often presented as a diagram that graphically presents the decomposition of work products.
Example 3-22

In Project A, the Project Manager prepared the Work Breakdown Structure of his project using decomposition techniques. sections.title_en: 3.2.7. Develop the Architecture Project Plan and Schedule
sections.title_zh: 编制架构项目计划与进度
sections.translation_zh:
详细范围确定后，可使用以下项目管理工具与技术来界定项目计划。此阶段建议编制进度；各阶段的详细进度应在“阶段规划”活动中编制（见 3.3 节）。

**1. 定义活动**

该活动用于识别为产出交付物而需执行的特定任务。

该流程的关键益处是把工作包分解为活动，为项目的估算、排程、执行、监控与控制提供基础 [PMBOK]。

在此流程中，项目经理应使用已编制的 WBS（它把交付物分解到更低层级，即工作包）。工作包在此流程中被分解为称为“活动”的更小组成部分，随后对活动排序与估算。

须说明，按项目管理方法，“工作包（work packages）”的定义与 TOGAF 标准（如 ADM 阶段 E）中的含义不同。为避免歧义，本章后文所用“工作包”均指上一段所述的项目管理含义。

> **示例 3-23**
>
> 在项目 A 中，项目经理使用工作分解结构中已定义的工作包，并将其分解为活动。“应用之间的关系与数据流”这一交付物的结果如下。

**2. 排列活动顺序**

该活动用于界定项目活动之间的全部关系。

该流程的关键益处是确定工作的逻辑顺序，从而在全部项目约束下获得最高效率 [PMBOK]。

请参考项目评估与审查技术（PERT），这是一种常用的、基于网络图的排序支持技术。

> **示例 3-24**
>
> 在项目 A 中，项目经理使用前导图法（Precedence Diagramming Method）为所有已定义活动排序。为此，项目经理使用了一款排程工具，以便轻松完成排序。对于最低层级的每项活动，项目经理都定义了前置活动，使所有任务都具有明确的依赖关系，从而能够构建进度。“应用之间的关系与数据流”这一交付物的结果如下。

**3. 估算活动资源与工期**

每个已识别活动都应就所需资源（如人力资源、设备）与工期（以估算资源完成该活动所需时间）进行估算。

关于以下常用工期估算技术，请参阅 PMBOK [PMBOK]：

- 专家判断；
- 类比估算；
- 参数估算；
- 三点估算；
- 群体决策技术；
- 储备分析。

> **示例 3-25**
>

**4. 制定进度**

source_units.text_en: 3.2.7. Develop the Architecture Project Plan and Schedule

After the detailed scope is defined, the following Project Management tools and techniques can be used in order to define the Project Plan. During this phase it is recommended to prepare a schedule; a detailed schedule for each phase should be prepared during the Planning a Stage activity (see Section 3.3).
1. Define Activities
This activity is used to identify any specific tasks that need to be executed in order to produce deliverables.
The key benefit of this process is to break down work packages into activities that provide a basis for estimating, scheduling, executing, monitoring, and controlling the project work [PMBOK].

In this process, the Project Manager should use the prepared Work Breakdown Structure that divides deliverables to the lower level; i.e., work packages. In this process work packages are decomposed into smaller components called activities, that will be later sequenced and estimated.

It should be clarified that in terms of the Project Management methods, the definition of “work packages” has a different meaning to the TOGAF Standard (e.g., in the ADM Phase E). In order to avoid ambiguity, later in this chapter we will use term “work packages” defined as in the previous paragraph.
Example 3-23

This activity is used to define all relationships between project activities.
